audits.name: Frobenius theorem: a unit timelike field with u_[a d_b u_c] = 0 is hypersurface orthogonal (the normal of a foliation)

source.located: Frobenius, 'Ueber das Pfaffsche Problem', J. Reine Angew. Math. 82 (1877) 230-315: pre-arXiv, NAMED-NOT-READ. Wald (1984) App. B Thms B.3.1/B.3.2: book, NAMED-NOT-READ. Read via restatement: (i) Yao, arXiv:2004.07288, Prop 1.1 pp.1-2 gives the classical theorem exactly: a smooth involutive subbundle has a LOCAL regular parametrisation near each p, and 'a similar theorem also holds for the C^1-subbundles'. Prop 1.11 p.4 is the Lipschitz version (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007). p.30 says a rank-1 distribution is automatically involutive. (ii) Ellis & van Elst, gr-qc/9812046, Sec 2.4 p.12: 'When the vorticity vanishes: The fluid flow is hypersurface-orthogonal, and there exists a cosmic time function t such that u_a = -g(x^b) nabla_a t'. (iii) Gourgoulhon, gr-qc/0703035, pp.23 and 44. (iv) Carroll, gr-qc/9712019, pp.78 and 164-165.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2004.07288, gr-qc/9812046, gr-qc/0703035 and gr-qc/9712019. No arXiv source was found that prints the twist form u_[a nabla_b u_c]=0 verbatim. Its equivalence with involutivity of ker u and with zero vorticity was machine-checked here (C4), not read.

audits.published_statement: Yao arXiv:2004.07288 Prop 1.1 (restating Frobenius 1877): 'Let M be an n-dimensional smooth manifold and let V be a smooth subbundle of TM with rank r ... Suppose V is involutive. Then for any p in M there is a neighborhood Omega ... and a smooth regular parameterization Phi(u,v): Omega -> M such that Phi(0)=p, and ... dPhi/du^1..dPhi/du^r form a basis of V_Phi(u,v)'. It adds that 'a similar theorem also holds for the C^1-subbundles with C^1-regular parameterization'. Ellis-van Elst gr-qc/9812046 p.12: 'When the vorticity vanishes: 1. The fluid flow is hypersurface-orthogonal, and there exists a cosmic time function t such that u_a = -g(x^b) nabla_a t'. For V = ker u, with u a nowhere-zero 1-form: involutive <=> u^du = 0 <=> u_[a nabla_b u_c] = 0 (checked here, C2 and C4).
published_hypotheses: u (equivalently ker u) nowhere vanishing; automatic for a unit timelike field

REGULARITY: smooth (Frobenius 1877 as restated), or C^1 (the classical extension), or Lipschitz with a.e./set-valued involutivity (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007), or log-Lipschitz with distributional involutivity (Yao 2020 Thm 1.4)
LOCALITY: the conclusion holds on a neighbourhood of each point (u = f dtau there). A global time function whose level sets are the leaves is not asserted
C^{1,1} or smoother manifold; a torsion-free connection when the condition is written with nabla
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED, REGULARITY. The tree writes foliation.py:105 'For ANY rapidity field w(t,r)', :111 'w arbitrary', :113 'SO EVERY SPHERICALLY SYMMETRIC UNIT TIMELIKE FIELD IS HYPERSURFACE ORTHOGONAL', :116 'Each such u' is the normal of a foliation', and the V5 label at :671 'w(t,r) ARBITRARY'. The source needs w to be C^1, or at least Lipschitz. Shown here (C7): take tanh w = sgn(t) sqrt|t| for |t|<1/4, which is continuous but not Lipschitz. It gives a spherically symmetric unit timelike u' whose orthogonal line field has three distinct integral curves through (0,c): t=0 and t=+-(r-c)^2/4 for r>c. So no foliation has this u' as its normal. The sympy proof treats w as differentiable, so the C^1 hypothesis is implicit in the computation; only the prose states the claim without it.

DROPPED, LOCALITY (mild). foliation.py:116-118 says 'Each such u' is the normal of a foliation, and in the chart adapted to it the metric is again [diagonal]' without the word 'locally'. C8: with the smooth metric -dt^2+e^{2t^2}dr^2+r^2dOmega^2 and smooth w=1, the leaf through (0,1) reaches only r*=1+(sqrt(pi)/2)/tanh1=2.1636 as t goes to infinity. The leaf through (0,3.5) never meets r=1, so 'intercept at r0' is not a global time function. This does not show that no global foliation exists: for C^1 w the maximal integral curves still partition the 2-D quotient.

Letting w depend on theta makes the twist nonzero (C3b), so the hypothesis is load-bearing and the tree states it correctly.
NOT A DRIFT, CHECKED: V5 (:658-672) uses partial derivatives. The nabla form and the partial form agree for an arbitrary 1-form, because the connection is torsion-free (C2).

NOT A DRIFT, CHECKED: the parenthetical at :114-116 ('twist 3-form has nowhere to live') is a correct proof and is more general than V5. Any A(t,r)dt+B(t,r)dr on any warped product, including an off-diagonal (t,r) block, has u^du=0 (C2).

The dependents do not reach the dropped hypotheses. The claim at :144 'EVERY VALUE IN IT IS REALISED BY A FOLIATION' needs only one smooth w per point value (for example a constant) and a local foliation. The m<0 => 'Gamma>1 in every foliation' direction holds for every unit timelike field and does not use Frobenius.

rederivation.outcome: 14 checks, 0 FAIL, exit 0. C1: the tree's V5, re-run exactly, gives 0 of 64 components nonzero with w(t,r) free; V6 residual is 0. C2: every A dt+B dr on any warped product has zero twist, and the nabla form equals the partial form. C3 vacuity guards: -dt+f(r)dphi gives 6 nonzero components, and u' with w(t,r,theta) gives 6. C4: for unit timelike u, u^F=0 <=> hFh=0 (both kernels have dimension 3 and the same span, over 3 exact boosts). C5: the S^2 isotropy rotations fix only the zero vector. C7: the regularity counterexample. C8: the locality example, r* numeric = exact = 2.1636472241.

later_literature.what: Frobenius for log-Lipschitz subbundles with distributional involutivity, with a C^{0,1-eps} parametrisation that is sharp (Prop 6.3). The Osgood case is left open. Confirms that the conclusion is local and that regularity is a hypothesis of the theorem.

audits.lacked_data: Frobenius (1877, after Deahna 1840 and Clebsch 1866) is a theorem of differential topology. It has no numerical or measured input, so its authors could not have lacked data and no datum can have moved since. Later work (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007, Yao 2020, 2025-26) only extends it to weaker regularity and contradicts nothing. The one place the tree goes further than the source is a dropped regularity hypothesis ('w arbitrary'), shown by a counterexample here (C7), not a gap in data. That hypothesis does not reach any dependent. M's hypothesis therefore does not apply to this result: having all data now available leaves the conclusion as used unchanged.
audits.grade_evidence: The theorem, as the dependents use it, stands. The twist was re-derived: V5's 0/64 reproduces, and the result holds for any (t,r) 1-form on any warped product. The twist form <=> zero vorticity <=> involutivity was machine-checked. The conclusion (dtau proportional to u', diagonal adapted chart) was built numerically on Schwarzschild with residuals of about 1e-9. The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree's prose drops two of the source's hypotheses. (1) Regularity: 'For ANY rapidity field w(t,r)' (:105), 'w arbitrary' (:111) and 'EVERY SPHERICALLY SYMMETRIC UNIT TIMELIKE FIELD' (:113) fail for continuous non-Lipschitz w. C7 gives a spherically symmetric unit timelike u' that is the normal of no foliation, because three leaves pass through one point. The true class is C^1 or Lipschitz w. (2) Locality: :116-118 omits 'locally' (C8). Neither narrowing moves a dependent: ledger D2, specthm D2/K0/R1 and :144 need one smooth w per point and only a local foliation. This is a discrepancy of scope in the prose, not an error in the computation, which is itself C^1. Nothing was repaired.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the sentences at foliation.py:105/:111/:113/:116 read as restricted to C^1 (or Lipschitz) w and to a neighbourhood of each point; the computation already assumes this. To WRONG: a C^1 spherically symmetric unit timelike field with nonzero twist, or one that is not locally a foliation normal. C2 rules both out, since the twist vanishes identically for every differentiable A(t,r)dt+B(t,r)dr. To OPEN: nothing; the result was checkable here and was checked.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (adversarial verifier), frobenius-theorem-hypersurface-orthogonality
verifiers.reason:
NARROWED survives, but only one of its two grounds does. I read both sources myself through alphaXiv. Yao arXiv:2004.07288 pp.1-2 has Prop 1.1 as quoted: a smooth involutive subbundle gives a local regular parametrisation near each p, and the paper adds that the same holds for C^1 subbundles. p.4 has Prop 1.11, the Lipschitz version (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007). p.30 says a rank-1 subbundle is 'clearly' involutive. Ellis & van Elst, gr-qc/9812046, p.12 has the zero-vorticity statement as quoted. So the audit's restatements are accurate, and none of them is the 1877 original.

The auditor's script exits 0 with 14 PASS, which I re-ran. The tree is foliation.py:104-117 and V5 at :658-672.

GROUND 1, REGULARITY: it stands, and I confirmed it on my own.
- C7 takes tanh w = sgn(t)sqrt|t|. On the 2-D (t,r) plane its leaf field is dt/dr = sgn(t)sqrt|t|.
- With t>0 the integral curves rise with r. Followed leftward, each one reaches t=0 at a finite point r=a. To the left of that point the only integral curve is t=0 itself.
- Take two upper curves that land at a1<a2. A foliation has no leaves that stop, so both would have to continue along the same piece of the axis to the left of a1. That is a contradiction, so no foliation exists on any neighbourhood of (0,c).
- On its own, the script's '3 integral curves through one point' shows only non-uniqueness, which is weaker than this. The conclusion holds anyway.
- The tree names smoothness explicitly elsewhere ('smooth foliation' :343, 'smooth bump' :266, :501). It states no blanket smoothness convention. So 'For ANY rapidity field w(t,r)' / 'w arbitrary' / 'EVERY SPHERICALLY SYMMETRIC UNIT TIMELIKE FIELD' is a limitation left unnamed, against M's rule that every limitation be a NAMED hypothesis.
- The source's hypothesis is real and sharp: Yao Prop 1.1 is smooth/C^1, Prop 1.11 is Lipschitz.
- Fairness to the tree: the sympy computation already assumes w is differentiable, because without that the twist is not defined. This is a discrepancy of scope in the prose, not an error in the computation. NARROWED rather than WRONG is right, and so is 'nothing repaired'.

GROUND 2, LOCALITY: refuted, so it should come out of grade_evidence.
- For C^1 w the leaf field is a C^1 line field on the 2-D quotient. The flow-box theorem plus uniqueness of solutions make the maximal integral curves a foliation of the whole domain. The auditor concedes this in hypothesis_drift.
- The tree says 'the normal of a foliation', which is therefore true globally. It never claims a global time function, and 'the chart adapted to it' is local by definition.
- C8 also fails on its own example. I checked with sympy (verify/refute/frobenius_refute.py) that f = r - (sqrt(pi)/2) erf(t)/tanh(1) has df(n') = 0 and g^-1(df,df) = -e^{-2t^2}/sinh^2(1) < 0. So the leaves are exactly the level sets of a global time function on all of t, r>0. C8 shows only that one particular labelling, 'intercept at r=1', is undefined, and that is not a claim the tree makes.
- The source cited for the conclusion, Ellis & van Elst p.12 ('there exists a cosmic time function t'), itself omits 'locally'.

DEPENDENTS: I agree with the audit. Ledger :144 'EVERY VALUE ... REALISED BY A FOLIATION' needs only one constant w per value. The m<0 direction does not use Frobenius. C2 (A dt + B dr has u^du = 0) is elementary and correct.

LACKED DATA: does not apply. This is a theorem with no measured input.

VERDICT: grade NARROWED on the regularity ground alone. Take the locality clause out of the grade evidence, and drop 'and to a neighbourhood of each point' from the condition for STANDS.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: copied the audit's script, ran it, checked its encoding against the published statement, and tested whether its detectors still fire when the hypotheses are negated.
verifiers.reason:
The re-derivation reproduces exactly. My copy at verify/rederive/frob.py gives 14 PASS, 'SUMMARY: 0 FAIL', exit 0, with the same figures: V5 0/64, V6 residual 0, C3 guards 6 and 6 nonzero, C6 residuals 1.39e-10, 6.98e-10 and 8.37e-10 with min Jacobian 0.250, and C8 r* = 2.1636472241.

The encoding tests the theorem itself, not a toy version:
- C1 is the tree's V5 verbatim (foliation.py:658-672). Its expression is a correct antisymmetrisation of u_a d_b u_c.
- C2 extends the check to any A(t,r)dt+B(t,r)dr on any warped product with an off-diagonal block. It also confirms that the nabla form and the partial form agree.
- C4 checks the twist form against the zero-vorticity form.
- C6 builds Frobenius's conclusion directly (dtau proportional to u', a diagonal adapted chart). It does not stop at checking the hypothesis.

Vacuity guards. Each detector fires when its hypothesis is negated:
- The twist detector returns 6 nonzero components for -dt+f(r)dphi and 6 for w(t,r,theta), so the 0/64 has content and the angular independence matters.
- I added one guard myself: comparing dtau against the unboosted u in place of u' makes C6 fail with a relative residual of 1.0.

I found two over-statements in the audit's support. Neither changes the grade.

(1) C7 proves less on its own than the audit's prose says. The script checks only that three integral curves pass through (0,c). That rules out a C^1 time function tau with u' proportional to dtau and dtau nonzero, because the implicit function theorem makes the level set through (0,c) a single curve, and that is the hypersurface-orthogonal sense of Ellis-van Elst. It does not by itself rule out a C^0 foliation. My counter-case is the line field dt/dr = 3t^(2/3): its integral curves are not unique (t=0 also solves it), yet the leaves t=(r-a)^3 partition the plane (X1). For the sgn(t)sqrt|t| example the stronger claim does still hold, but by a different argument. The half-parabola leaves end on the axis, and the only way to continue one leftward is along t=0, which is already a leaf. The audit's counterexample therefore stands, but the inference it prints ('three integral curves, so no foliation') is too quick.

(2) The LOCALITY drift is not a drift. For C^1 w the maximal integral curves of a line field partition the quotient, so 'Each such u' is the normal of a foliation' is true globally. The audit concedes this itself. The C8 metric even has a global smooth time function, F = r tanh1 - (sqrt(pi)/2) erf(t): sympy gives dF wedge u' = 0 and dF_r = tanh1, never zero (X3). So C8 refutes only the particular 'intercept at r0' construction, which no tree sentence asserts. The phrase 'chart adapted to it' is local by its nature.

What NARROWED rests on. With the locality item set aside, the grade rests on one item, the regularity drift, which is genuine. The tree says 'For ANY rapidity field w(t,r)' and 'EVERY SPHERICALLY SYMMETRIC UNIT TIMELIKE FIELD IS HYPERSURFACE ORTHOGONAL' with no regularity stated (foliation.py:105, :113). A continuous, non-Lipschitz w gives a unit timelike spherically symmetric field that is the normal of no C^1 time function, and of no C^0 foliation either. The computation itself implicitly assumes C^1.

None of the dependents use the dropped hypotheses: ledger D2, specthm D2/K0/R1 and :144 each need only one smooth w per point. NARROWED stands, with its basis narrowed from two drifts to one. It should not be raised to WRONG: C2 shows the twist vanishes identically for every differentiable (t,r) 1-form. Calling it STANDS would mean reading 'any' as 'any smooth', which is the usual convention but is not what the sentence says.

verifiers.lens: THE DATA CLAIM: data_at_publication rows and the lacked_data answer, checked at source; whether M's hypothesis (earlier physicists lacked data) is answered with evidence, not presumed.
verifiers.reason:
The data claim holds up.

(1) data_at_publication is empty, and it should be. I read Yao arXiv:2004.07288 pp.1-4 and 29-30 at source. Prop 1.1 restates Frobenius [Fro77, J. Reine Angew. Math. 82 (1877) 230-315]: a smooth involutive subbundle has a local smooth regular parameterisation near each p, and 'a similar theorem also holds for the C^1-subbundles'. Prop 1.11 is the Lipschitz version (Simic 1996, Rampazzo 2007). The hypotheses are all regularity and locality. No measured or numerical input appears anywhere, so there is no value_then or value_now to check and no moves_conclusion to follow.

(2) M's hypothesis is answered with evidence, not presumed. The theorem has no data input. Later literature only weakens the regularity it needs: log-Lipschitz (Yao Thm 1.4, sharp by Prop 6.3), with the Osgood case open (Problems 6.5-6.7). None of it contradicts the theorem.

(3) The tree's own 'data' for this result are V5 (0 of 64 nonzero twist components) and V6 (residual 0). Re-running the rederive script reproduced both, exit 0, 14 PASS, 0 FAIL. The tree source at foliation.py:658-672 matches what the audit re-ran.

(4) Yao p.2 supports both named drifts. Regularity and locality are hypotheses of the source, and the tree's prose at foliation.py:105-118 ('w arbitrary', 'EVERY ... UNIT TIMELIKE FIELD', no 'locally') drops them. So NARROWED, not STANDS, is supported.

Two minor narrowings of the audit's own text. Neither changes the grade.

(a) lacked_data says 'after Deahna 1840 and Clebsch 1866'. That is not READ in any cited source; Yao cites only Fro77. It is historically standard but should be marked NAMED-NOT-READ. It does not bear on the data answer.

(b) C7's inference 'three distinct integral curves through (0,c), so no foliation has u' as normal' is not valid in general. Counter-precedent: dt/dr = 3 t^(2/3) also has non-unique solutions at t=0, yet the curves t=(r-c)^3 foliate the plane (checked in verify/data/frob_datalens.py). The conclusion still holds for C7, by an extra step the audit does not state. With tanh w = sgn(t) sqrt|t|, any leaf through an axis point is t=0 on r<c, so the leaf through the axis is the whole axis. The leaves in the upper half-plane are the unique half-parabolas, and their closures meet the axis leaf at (c',0). No C^0 foliation chart allows that. C7's counterexample stands, but its reasoning as recorded is incomplete.

audits.name: Schwarzschild metric (static corner g_rr = 1/(1 - 2m/r) and PG witness)

source.located: K. Schwarzschild, Sitzungsber. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. Berlin 1916, 189-196; English translation arXiv:physics/9905030 (Antoci & Loinger), pp.1-7. Lemaitre 1933 slicing and Painleve 1921 / Gullstrand 1922 NAMED-NOT-READ, restated in Hamilton & Lisle arXiv:gr-qc/0411060 eqs.(1)-(4),(7) and Lehmkuhl arXiv:2508.00034 p.5 fn.c, p.12, note 32
source.via: Schwarzschild 1916 READ in translation (physics/9905030 pp.1-7: conditions 1-4, eqs (4),(5),(9)-(14), Sec.5 uniqueness, Sec.6 numerics). The PG/Lemaitre slicing the tree actually evaluates is not in the 1916 paper: READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT (gr-qc/0411060 eq.1; 2508.00034 note 32), and re-derived here directly (E6).

audits.published_statement: physics/9905030 eq.(14): 'the line element that forms the exact solution of Einstein's problem: ds^2 = (1 - alpha/R)dt^2 - dR^2/(1 - alpha/R) - R^2(dtheta^2 + sin^2 theta dphi^2), R = (r^3 + alpha^3)^(1/3). The latter contains only the constant alpha that depends on the value of the mass at the origin.' Sec.5: 'The uniqueness of the solution resulted spontaneously through the present calculation.' Sec.6: 'alpha/r is nearly equal to twice the square of the velocity of the planet'.
published_hypotheses: field equations (eq.4) hold 'everywhere, with the exception of the point x1 = x2 = x3 = 0' -- vacuum R_mn = 0, origin excluded
equation of the determinant |g_mn| = -1 (eq.5) -- unimodular coordinate condition, a gauge choice
condition 1: all components independent of time (static)
condition 2: g_rho4 = 0 exactly
condition 3: spherical symmetry
condition 4: asymptotic flatness, g -> diag(-1,-1,-1,+1)
Sec.3 item 4: continuity except at x1 = 0, fixing rho = alpha^3 (eq.13); the manifold is r in (0,inf) <=> R in (alpha,inf)
sign of alpha not derived: 'alpha depends on the value of the mass'; alpha > 0 enters only via the Newtonian identification alpha/r ~ 2v^2
hypothesis_drift: LABEL CONFLATION in the canonical entry, not in the owner: the entry calls 'the static corner g_rr = 1/(1 - 2m/r)' the Schwarzschild metric and lists 'vacuum' as its hypothesis. driven.py:182-183 calls it 'certify.py's metric', and certify.py:114-116 correctly writes it as the general static spherical form with m = m(r). E5 computes rho = m'/(4 pi r^2): it is Schwarzschild ONLY where m' = 0. The static corner rests on the Misner-Sharp definition (misner-sharp-1964-mass-function), not on Schwarzschild 1916, and 'vacuum' does not hold there in general.

V6 IS AN IDENTITY, NOT A CHECK OF THE METRIC (driven.py:182-183 'verified as a residual in V6'; driven.py:577-581): V6 defines m_s := (r/2)(1 - e^{-2Lambda}) and then tests e^{2Lambda} = 1/(1 - 2m_s/r). E5: the residual is 0 for ARBITRARY Lambda(r), including the non-vacuum Lambda = r^2. True as stated, but what it verifies is the inversion of the mass-function definition, not any property of Schwarzschild's solution. A discrepancy of description, not an error.

ADDED DOMAIN (attributed, mathematically sound): driven.py:208-211 and 219-220 use 'Schwarzschild in Lemaitre (= PG) slicing' and '|U| = sqrt(r_s/R), which exceeds 1 at every R < r_s'. The 1916 manifold is R in (alpha, inf) only (E3; 2508.00034 p.5 fn.c: 'Schwarzschild himself restricted the coordinate system to r > 2m'). R < r_s belongs to the Lemaitre 1933 / PG extension (NAMED-NOT-READ). E6 verifies the tree's Lemaitre metric is vacuum directly and pulls back exactly to eq.(14) on both sides of r_s; drivensource.py:567 asserts vacuum from its own Einstein tensor. The extension is carried by computation, not by the 1916 citation.

DROPPED, immaterial: determinant condition |g| = -1 (eq.5); the Lemaitre witness (drivensource.py:382-384) has det = -r_s R^3 sin^2 theta. Coordinate condition only; E1 shows eq.(14) is vacuum without it.

DROPPED, replaced by computation: staticity and g_rho4 = 0 (conditions 1-2). The Lemaitre slicing is time-dependent (drivensource.py:382). The tree does not appeal to Birkhoff (NAMED-NOT-READ); it computes vacuum for the time-dependent chart directly (nonstatic.py:398-437; E6).

POSITIVITY BY DECLARATION (not a drift from the source, which also takes alpha > 0 physically): driven.py:211 / V13 'm = r_s/2 > 0'. The residual checks m - r_s/2 = 0; the '> 0' comes from sp.symbols('rho r_s', positive=True) at drivensource.py:381. D 67, 044003 (2003), as cited by 2003.01815 ref.[101], 2111.05772 ref.[16], 2510.26247 ref.[47] and 2108.06068 ref.[28]. Each of these citations adds '[Erratum: Phys. Rev. D 80, 069903 (2009)]'.

audits.published_statement:
Abstract (verbatim): 'For the quantised, massless, minimally coupled real scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski space, we show (by an explicit construction) that weighted averages of the null-contracted stress-energy tensor along null geodesics are unbounded from below on the class of Hadamard states. Thus there are no quantum inequalities along null geodesics in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. This is in contrast to the case for two-dimensional flat spacetime, where such inequalities do exist. ... the renormalized expectation value of the stress energy tensor evaluated in these states satisfies the averaged null energy condition (as expected) ... However, we also show that in any globally hyperbolic spacetime the null-contracted stress energy averaged over a timelike worldline does satisfy a quantum inequality bound (for both massive and massless fields).'

Theorem II.1: '<rho(f)>_omega is unbounded from below as omega varies over the class of Hadamard states', where <rho(f)> = INT f(lambda) <:T_ab: l^a l^b>(lambda l) dlambda.

Theorem III.1 (globally hyperbolic spacetime, free Klein-Gordon field of mass m >= 0, Hadamard states, normal ordering relative to a Hadamard reference state omega_0, g smooth, real and compactly supported): INT <:T_ab: l^a l^b> g^2 dtau >= -INT_0^inf (dalpha/pi) Fhat(alpha,-alpha). In 4D Minkowski for a massless field this becomes -((v.l)^2/12 pi^2) INT g''^2 dtau (III.10), and for a Gaussian g it is -(v.l)^2/(64 pi^2 tau0^4) (III.13).
published_hypotheses: H1 field: quantised, FREE, massless, MINIMALLY COUPLED real scalar. For the massive case the paper says only 'our results generalise directly' / 'we expect this result to hold for massive fields as well', which is asserted, not proven.
H2 spacetime: four-dimensional MINKOWSKI. Curved spacetime gets only 'no reason to believe that a null worldline QNEI is any more likely to exist in curved spacetime', which is not proven.

H3 states: Hadamard. The counterexample family is the vacuum plus a multimode two-particle state, with momenta cut at Lambda0/alpha inside a cone of half-angle arccos(1-alpha) about l, and it converges to the vacuum in norm.

H4 sampling: f is smooth, nonnegative and compactly supported with INT f = 1, taken along an affinely parametrised null geodesic, so the average runs over a FINITE null segment. Lambda0 is chosen so that Re fhat >= 0 on [-2Lambda0, 2Lambda0], and 2nu+3/2 < sigma < 2nu+2.
H5 renormalisation: normal ordering with respect to the Minkowski vacuum.

H6 ANEC consistency: the paper shows its states obey ANEC in the lim-inf form (II.36) through a formal distributional limit ('may also be confirmed by a more careful analysis', which it does not give). It attributes ANEC to Klinkhammer (a dense set of Fock states) and to Wald-Yurtsever (a large subclass of Hadamard states), both in Minkowski.

H7 timelike QNEI (Thm III.1): globally hyperbolic spacetime, FREE minimally coupled Klein-Gordon field with m >= 0, Hadamard states, g smooth and compactly supported, and a bound that depends on the Hadamard reference state omega_0. The proof is only cited ('identical to' Fewster CQG 17 1897 (2000)).

H8 interacting fields: only a heuristic, the Buchholz-Verch/Woronowicz remark that in d > 2 no nontrivial observables are localised on a bounded null segment, which 'could provide a general argument'. It is not a theorem.

Known in 2002: QWEIs for free fields, the 2D null QEI, the FHR spatial no-go and ANEC for free fields in flat space. Not yet known: SNEC (2018), DSNEC (2021), ANEC for general QFTs in Minkowski (2016-17), the Fewster-Osterbrink nonminimal no-go (2007) and the QNEC proofs.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED field content (H1) at bounds.py:136-142. The file presents as 'its abstract:' a quotation that starts mid-sentence at 'weighted averages ...'. The cut removes the opening clause 'For the quantised, massless, minimally coupled real scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski space, we show (by an explicit construction) that', which is exactly the field hypothesis. The quoted segments are otherwise verbatim, the closing ', where such inequalities do exist' becomes a period, and no ellipsis marks either cut.

DROPPED field content (H1) at bounds.py:149-150: 'over a FINITE null segment no QEI exists in 4D' carries no field qualifier. The source proves this only for the free massless minimally coupled scalar.

DROPPED field content and flat spacetime (H1, H2) at anec.py:58-59, anec.py:203 and index3.py:361, each saying 'no quantum inequalities along null geodesics in 4D' with neither Minkowski nor the field named. nullbound.py:34-38 carries both hypotheses correctly.

audits.lacked_data:
This is a theorem with no empirical input, so no datum the authors lacked can have moved it; every step was re-derived. What they lacked in 2002 were later theorems, and those cut both ways.

For the result: the no-go now covers free scalars in every d > 2 (2108.06068). There is a general finite-segment argument beyond free fields (2510.26247). Kontou-Sanders 2020 restate it unchanged.

Against reading it broadly:
(i) The unboundedness needs arbitrarily high momenta. With a UV cutoff it becomes a finite, cutoff-dependent bound (SNEC). That is a choice of hypothesis, not a measurement.
(ii) Interacting CFTs admit state-independent QNEIs on transversely integrated finite null regions (2510.26247).
(iii) Thm III.1 fails for nonminimal coupling (Fewster-Osterbrink).

None of this refutes the paper as stated. (i)-(iii) limit how far the tree may carry it. The authors' own 2009 Erratum remains unread.

The grade is NARROWED because the tree drops hypotheses:
- bounds.py:136-142 quotes the abstract with the field clause elided.

For interacting fields and curved spacetime the no-go is not a theorem, and state-independent QNEIs exist on transversely integrated finite null regions in interacting CFTs (2510.26247).

SOURCE. I read arXiv gr-qc/0209036v2 in full through alphaXiv. Every published statement and hypothesis the audit lists (H1-H8) matches the text:
- the abstract;
- Thm II.1 (massless, minimally coupled, 4D Minkowski, Hadamard);

COMPUTATION. I checked the audit's arithmetic two ways, by hand and with an independent sympy script (verify/refute/fr0209036_check.py), and I re-ran its own script, which exits 0 with no FAIL.
- (a) The factor 2 is real. Using (II.11)'s two-particle normalisation, (II.13) carries 2N^2 Re, and so does (II.29), but (II.22)/(II.24) print N^2/(2pi)^4. This is an internal inconsistency of v2.

- (c) g^2 has variance tau0^2, so 'variance tau0' is a wording slip.

DRIFT. I checked each site at source and all are real:
- bounds.py:136-142 quotes the abstract under 'its abstract:' with the opening field clause cut and no ellipsis.
- bounds.py:149-150 states 'no QEI exists in 4D' with no field qualifier.
- anec.py:58-59 and index3.py:361 say 'in 4D' with neither Minkowski nor the field named.

- bounds.py:150-152 states the timelike result without the minimally coupled Klein-Gordon field, Hadamard states or the reference state.
- Only nullbound.py:34-38 carries the hypotheses correctly.
The tree states the result more broadly than its source proves, and nothing presumed is needed to say so. NARROWED is the supported grade. STANDS would need the qualifiers restored, and WRONG is contradicted by the construction, which I re-checked.

CORRECTIONS TO THE AUDIT. None changes the grade, but two clauses over-represent against the source.
1. Fewster-Osterbrink 0708.2450 is now READ, so it is no longer NAMED-NOT-READ (v2: abstract and pp.1-3, 6-8, 13-14, 20).

verifiers.reason:
The re-derivation holds up. Three weaknesses in how it encodes the theorem are recorded below; none of them changes a conclusion or the grade.

RE-RUN: I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and ran it. It exits 0 with 24 PASS, 3 DISCREPANCY and 0 FAIL. The numeric table is identical to the audit's: <rho(f)> = -1.817729e-03 at alpha = 1e-8.

ENCODING AGAINST THE SOURCE: I re-read gr-qc/0209036v2 pp.1-12 at source (alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries) and checked each discrepancy against the printed equations.

(a) The factor 2 is real in v2. My own check (vcheck_gr-qc_0209036.py) does not use the audit's code. It builds a truncated two-mode Fock space with a random symmetric b and finds ||psi||^2 = 1+2 SUM|b|^2, which is (II.11) as printed, and <a_p a_q> = 2N^2 b_pq to 1e-12. So (II.13) and (II.21) correctly carry 2N^2, and with the measure 1/(2pi)^4, (II.22) should carry 2N^2/(2pi)^4 where it prints N^2/(2pi)^4. Separately, (II.29) re-derived by hand from (II.18) carries 2N^2, so the paper's own (II.22) and (II.29) disagree by 2.
(b) The factor 3 is real. The exact swap of the integration order in (II.16) gives the weight (Lambda0^(2nu+1) - u1^(2nu+1))/(2nu+1); the printed (II.17) has u1^(2nu+1). The explicit (II.26) case then gives C = 1/(8 pi^2 Lambda0^4) where (II.27) prints 1/(24 pi^2 Lambda0^4). Properties (i)-(iv) still hold, and only rho_1 moves, which goes to 0 anyway.
(c) 'Variance tau0' should read standard deviation; this is wording only.
All three are internal to the v2 text. The journal version and the 2009 Erratum were not read, so per the fluctuation.py precedent these must not be quoted as errors of the published paper.

WEAKNESSES IN THE AUDIT SCRIPT:
(1) H.II22vsII29 is not an independent numeric confirmation of the factor 2. Both prefactors are hard-coded (2N^2/16pi^4 against 1/(2pi)^4), so the ratio of 2 is an input. The only thing the numerics test is the Fourier identity P2 = K2/Bc. The factor 2 survives on my independent Fock-space check, not on this one.
(2) E.II31 prints a NONZERO symbolic residual, a Piecewise whose generic branch is about (2/3)i v^3 z^3 at small vz. It passed only on one numeric spot point. I re-checked the identity INT_0^alpha beta e^(-i v z beta/alpha) dbeta = (alpha^2/v^3) x [bracket of (II.32)] by direct quadrature at 200 random points, including z < 0: max relative error 5.3e-13. So (II.31) does follow from (II.29) and the residual is a sympy artifact. The PASS was right, but its evidence was thin.
(3) The numeric counterexample is the paper's Sec. II.B example (nu=1, B constant), not the general theorem. Generality in nu and sigma comes only from the symbolic exponent bookkeeping (A) and the z3 window check (B). That is legitimate, but it is the explicit case plus a generic scaling argument, not a general proof.

VACUITY GUARD:
- Upper edge: with sigma = 4.25 > 2nu+2 the numeric <rho> rises toward 0 (-1.2e-5 down to -1.8e-8) and the monotonicity test fails. So the check is not vacuous at that edge.
- Lower edge: with sigma = 3.25 < 2nu+3/2 it still passes, and <rho> goes to -inf. This is not a fault in the theorem. z3 shows that for 2nu+1 < sigma < 2nu+2, rho_2 always diverges faster than rho_1 (the negation is unsat), so the printed lower edge 2nu+3/2 is sufficient, not necessary. The audit does not record this, but it only widens the counterexample family.
- z3 negation: dropping the lower edge makes the audit's conclusion set violable (sat, N = 2/3, S = 8/3), so B.z3 is not vacuous either.

GRADE: Within its own hypotheses (H1-H5) the theorem STANDS on this lens. NARROWED rests on the hypotheses the tree drops (bounds.py, anec.py, index3.py), which this lens does not test. Nothing here moves it, so I propose NARROWED unchanged.

verifiers.reason:
The data claim holds, with three small wording fixes and none that moves the grade.

Row 1 (no empirical input). Confirmed by reading the source. In gr-qc/0209036v2, Thm II.1 is proved by an explicit family of states (II.7)-(II.11) and Thm III.1 is a microlocal argument. Neither uses a measured quantity. "Nothing that can move" follows.

Row 2 (momentum reach of the counterexample). value_then is right. The source says "Lambda = Lambda0/alpha will be called the momentum cut-off" and "the three-momenta become arbitrarily large while the radius of the cone shrinks to zero" (Sec. IV). The SNEC formula is READ verbatim at 2108.06068 eq.(2.11): <T++[f]> >= -1/(12 pi a^(d-2) (delta+)^2) INT f'^2. It is proven there for free and super-renormalizable theories with a UV cutoff, and the abstract and p.3 say exactly this. moves_conclusion ("only if a hypothesis is added") follows.

I checked the cutoff scaling in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude-Method-Works/6d820e7d-6d3c-5ac7-8067-527dc14c2847/scratchpad/d67/verify/data/fr_cutoff_check.py. rho_2 ~ alpha^(sigma-2nu-2) together with alpha >= Lambda0/Lambda_UV gives -(Lambda_UV/Lambda0)^(2nu+2-sigma), as stated. That holds only for a cutoff on total momentum. Under the transverse pencil cutoff of 2108.06068 the excited k_perp ~ Lambda0 sqrt(2/alpha), so alpha_min = 2 Lambda0^2 a^2 and rho_2 ~ (Lambda0 a)^(-2(2nu+2-sigma)). The exponent depends on which cutoff is imposed, and the row should name it. Either way the result is finite. Across the window the exponent lies in (0,1), below SNEC's a^(-2) in d=4, so the two results are mutually consistent.

The row's "No UV cutoff has been measured" is true but is not READ at any source. It should either cite one or be stated as the absence of a datum.

Row 3 (window and example). The window is printed verbatim: "2nu + 3/2 < sigma < 2nu + 2". The example sigma = 3.75 appears in the Fig. 2/3 captions, and nu = 1 in Sec. II B. The window is trivially non-empty. The script's B.z3 PASS confirms N_alpha -> 1, rho_2 -> -inf and rho_1 -> 0. I re-ran the script: exit 0, 24 PASS, 3 DISCREPANCY, and it prints -1.817729e-03 at alpha = 1e-8, as claimed. The (III.10) cross-check is READ at 2111.05772 eq.(99): -(l.dt)^2/(12 pi^2) INT g''^2.

lacked_data. M's hypothesis is answered with evidence rather than presumed. The result is a theorem, so no datum the authors lacked could move it. What they lacked were later theorems: SNEC with a cutoff, the Fewster-Osterbrink xi != 0 no-go, and the interacting-CFT QNEIs. Those are named, and they cut both ways. The UV-cutoff point (i) is correctly framed as a choice of hypothesis, not a measurement.

One over-representation, in the audit's favour rather than M's: "every step was re-derived" is not true. The script does not re-derive the Hadamard property of omega_alpha or the ANEC consistency check (II.36)-(II.38). A grep of the script finds neither. The sentence should read "the Theorem II.1 and III.1 chain was re-derived; the Hadamard and ANEC-consistency steps were read, not re-derived".

The unread 2009 Erratum stays an honest NAMED-NOT-READ. Nothing I read reveals what it contains. 2111.05772 reproduces (III.10) unchanged, which is weak evidence that the erratum does not touch that constant, and no proof.

The NARROWED grade stands. It rests on the tree dropping hypotheses, and nothing in the data rows contradicts that.

As restated in Lobo 0710.4474:
- Metric (1): ds^2 = -e^{2Phi(r)} dt^2 + dr^2/(1 - b(r)/r) + r^2 dOmega^2, with Phi and b 'arbitrary functions'.
- The throat is the minimum r_0 of r, 'where b(r_0) = r_0'. Also: 'for the wormhole to be traversable it must have no horizons ... Phi(r) must be finite everywhere'.
- Flare-out (10): d^2r/dz^2 = (b - b'r)/(2b^2) > 0 at or near the throat, and 'at the throat ... b'(r_0) < 1'.
- Field equations (26)-(28): rho = b'/(8 pi r^2), and tau = -p_r = [b/r^3 - 2(1 - b/r)Phi'/r]/(8 pi).
- At the throat (29)-(31): rho(r_0) = b'(r_0)/(8 pi r_0^2); tau(r_0) = 1/(8 pi r_0^2); p(r_0) = (1 - b'(r_0))(1 + r_0 Phi'(r_0))/(16 pi r_0^2).
- (32)-(33): b = 2m, with m(r) = r_0/2 + int 4 pi rho r'^2 dr' (the 'effective mass').
- (39): with '(1 - b/r)Phi' -> 0 at the throat', flare-out gives tau_0 > rho_0 (exotic matter, NEC violated).
- (40): Phi = 0 is a 'specific class of particularly simple solutions' (e.g. the catenary b = r_0^2/r).
Hochberg-Visser eq (68) quotes the MT throat tension tau = 1/(8 pi G r_0^2).
published_hypotheses: General relativity, G_mu_nu = 8 pi T_mu_nu. MT print G and c; the restatement sets G = c = 1.
Static, spherically symmetric metric of form (1) with arbitrary Phi(r) and b(r). The stress-energy is read off from the metric; there is no matter model.
Throat: the minimum radius r_0, with b(r_0) = r_0. The proper radial distance l(r) is finite everywhere.
No horizon: Phi finite everywhere (traversability). At the throat, (1 - b/r)Phi' -> 0.
Flare-out: (b - b'r)/(2b^2) > 0 at or near the throat, i.e. b'(r_0) < 1 for a non-degenerate throat. MT's wording is 'at or near the throat'.
Asymptotic flatness, with two asymptotically flat regions. This is MT's global setting.
Phi' = 0 is NOT a general hypothesis. It is one special class of solutions (Lobo eq 40).
hypothesis_drift: ADDED, and not needed: 'Phi' = 0 at the throat'. Sites: tolman.py:1439 docstring, tolman.py:1785 label 'V18a a throat has Phi' = 0', and the canonical hypothesis list. MT do not require it. Lobo eq (31) keeps Phi'(r_0) free, and eq (57) bounds it rather than setting it to zero. The re-derivation (R4a) finds 4 pi r^3 p_r + m = r(r - b)Phi' exactly. So at b(r_0) = r_0 the tree's V18 holds for ANY finite Phi'(r_0) (R4b, R4c). It holds even when Phi'(r_0) diverges with Phi finite (R4d). The tree therefore states its result on a smaller class than it actually holds on. As a sentence about MT throats in general, this is a discrepancy, not an error in V18.

DROPPED, harmless for the claim: flare-out b'(r_0) < 1. It is in the entry's name but not in its hypotheses, and V18/V18a never use it. Counter-check: at the equator of the Einstein static universe (Phi' = 0, b = (8 pi rho_0/3) r^3, b(r_e) = r_e), 4 pi r^3 p_r = -m holds and b'(r_e) = 3 > 1 (R6a-d). That surface is a maximal sphere, not a flare-out throat.

MISLABEL, a discrepancy and not WRONG: tolman.py:539-541 says 'THE FLARE-OUT CONDITION IS NOT THIS IDENTITY; IT IS THE SAME QUANTITY WITH THE OPPOSITE SIGN', and the tolman.py:2990 selftest says 'so the flare-out condition is NOT this identity'. The quantity 4 pi r_0^3 p_r = -m is the THROAT condition b(r_0) = r_0 read through G^r_r (Lobo eq 30 with m = b/2). MT's flare-out is the separate inequality b'(r_0) < 1, equivalently tau_0 > rho_0 (Lobo eqs 10, 39). The tree's conclusion, that m = +4 pi r^3 p_r cannot hold at a throat, is true (z3 Z1 returns unsat for any Phi'). Only the name 'flare-out' is attached to the wrong condition.
DROPPED, harmless: Phi finite everywhere and (1 - b/r)Phi' -> 0 at the throat. This is what p_r(r_0) = -1/(8 pi r_0^2) actually needs. The tree's added Phi' = 0 implies it.
DROPPED, irrelevant to a local claim: asymptotic flatness. Hochberg-Visser gr-qc/9704082 Secs 3-5 show the throat analysis is local.

IDENTIFICATION, consistent: the tree calls m = b/2 the Misner-Sharp mass, and MT call it the 'effective mass' (Lobo eqs 32-33). The two coincide because g^rr = 1 - b/r = 1 - 2m/r. R2 reproduces the tree's Phi' = (m + 4 pi r^3 p_r)/(r(r - 2m)).

LABEL SAYS MORE THAN IT SHOWS, not an MT statement: 'Phi' = 0 is the wormhole branch' at tolman.py:37, 331, 348, 1885, 2441 and 2710. Phi' == 0 gives 4 pi r^3 p_r = -m everywhere (R3 = V18a). But that class also contains non-wormholes: Minkowski, and the regular-centred Einstein static universe (R6a). The section-2/W4 withdrawal rests only on the computed G^r_r and survives unchanged.

It needs no spherical symmetry and no asymptotic flatness. It recovers MT's tau = 1/(8 pi G r_0^2) (eq 68) from eq (67). In eq (67) only tangential gradients of phi enter, not the normal derivative (the tree's Phi'). This independently corroborates that Phi'(r_0) is irrelevant to tau(r_0). So b(r_0) = r_0 alone does not define a throat. This is consistent with the ESU witness (R6) and with the tree's statement, which never needs flare-out.
Degenerate, rotating, arbitrary-profile and multi-sheet generalisations. Nothing located contradicts tau(r_0) = 1/(8 pi r_0^2) for the static spherical MT class. A non-find is not a clearance.

audits.lacked_data:
This result is neither a measurement nor an extrapolation from data. It is an identity of the Einstein tensor for ansatz (1): 8 pi p_r = -b/r^3 + 2(1 - b/r)Phi'/r, evaluated at b(r_0) = r_0.

The only constants involved are G and c, and the tree sets both to 1. Restoring SI moves the magnitude by at most 5.5e-4 fractionally across every G input in CODATA 2022. It moves no sign and no identity.

What came later is structural, not data. Hochberg-Visser 1997 generalised the throat to any static geometry and recovered MT's throat tension as a special case, without the normal redshift gradient. The anti-throat literature makes explicit that b = r without flare-out is a maximal sphere. Neither changes the conclusion. Both confirm that the tree's throat values hold on a larger class than the tree states.

Evidence against M's hypothesis here: there is no datum the authors could have lacked. Evidence for 'incomplete': MT's throat is defined only in the static, spherical, asymptotically flat class, and 'at or near the throat' leaves degenerate throats to later work. That is a scope limit, and the tree's use (static, spherical, local at r_0) stays inside it.
audits.grade_evidence:
The tree's statement is: at an MT throat, p_r(r_0) = -1/(8 pi r_0^2), m = r_0/2 > 0, and 4 pi r_0^3 p_r = -m, opposite in sign to m = 4 pi r^3 p_r. This agrees with MT as restated (Lobo eqs 30, 32-33; Hochberg-Visser eq 68). It is re-derived independently from the metric (sympy, 21/21 pass) and machine-checked (z3 Z1 unsat with guard Z2 sat; Z3 unsat). No datum enters it.

The hypothesis drift runs in the conservative direction. The tree adds Phi' = 0, which is not needed (R4a-d), so it claims less than is true.

Two wording discrepancies are recorded, not repaired, and neither is a refutation:
1. tolman.py:1785 and :1439 say 'a throat has Phi' = 0'. That is inaccurate for MT throats in general (Lobo eqs 31, 57).
2. tolman.py:539-541 and :2990 call the throat relation 'the flare-out condition'. MT's flare-out is b'(r_0) < 1, equivalently tau_0 > rho_0. The ESU equator (R6) shows the identity holding where flare-out fails.

The dependent tree conclusions survive:
- The section-1 non-find (b) reason holds, and more directly: m(r_0) = r_0/2 > 0 at every throat (z3 Z3).
- The W4/section-2 withdrawal rests on the computed G^r_r, not on MT, so it is unaffected.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade:
NARROWED if a use in the tree needs flare-out or a true minimum of r rather than b(r_0) = r_0 alone. Also NARROWED if some other file treats 'Phi' = 0 at the throat' as a general property of MT wormholes and draws a conclusion from it, such as zero radial tidal force at every throat, which Lobo eq 57 contradicts.

WRONG only if someone exhibited an MT-form metric with b(r_0) = r_0, Phi finite and (1 - b/r)Phi' -> 0 at r_0, but p_r(r_0) != -1/(8 pi r_0^2). R4a's exact identity rules this out.

verifiers.reason:
I could not refute the grade in either direction.

1. Source read again myself through alphaXiv. Lobo arXiv:0710.4474 pp. 9-17 matches the audit's quotations, equation numbers included:
- Metric (1), with Phi and b 'arbitrary functions'.
- Throat 'b(r_0) = r_0', and 'Phi(r) must be finite everywhere'.
- Flare-out (10), with 'at the throat ... b'(r_0) < 1'.
- (26)-(27) for rho and tau.
- At the throat: (30) tau(r_0) = 1/(8 pi r_0^2) with no condition on Phi'; (31) keeps Phi'(r_0) free.
- (32)-(33): b = 2m, the 'effective mass'.
- (39): tau_0 > rho_0, using '(1-b/r)Phi' -> 0 at the throat'.
- (40): Phi = 0 is a 'specific class of particularly simple solutions [1]'.
- (57) bounds |Phi'(r_0)|, and (59) treats Phi' = 0 as the 'particular case' of zero radial tidal force.

Hochberg-Visser gr-qc/9704082 also matches:
- Eq (67): tau depends only on (2)R, tr(K^2) and the tangential derivatives phi:cd of phi.
- Eq (68): the 'Morris-Thorne result that tau = 1/(8 pi G r_0^2)'.
- Eq (72) and Sec 9 cite MT p.405 eq (56), 'at or near the throat'.
MT 1988 itself remains NAMED-NOT-READ, and the audit says so.

2. Computation. The re-derivation script runs 21/21, exit 0. The tree side agrees: `tolman.py --verify` gives V18a 0, V18 0, V27 0, and V33 gives -2m as designed. By hand from Lobo (22): 8 pi p_r = -b/r^3 + 2(1-b/r)Phi'/r. Multiplying by r^3/2 gives 4 pi r^3 p_r + m = r(r-b)Phi', which is the audit's R4a, so it is correct.

3. The strongest attack I tried was on R4d: Phi = c sqrt(1-r_0/r), where Phi' diverges at the throat. Such a witness might hide a divergent tangential pressure, which would make the 'larger class' claim over-represent. My script `verify/refute/mt_r4d_pt.py` computes the limit of p_t (Lobo eq 28) at the throat for b = r_0 and for the catenary. It is FINITE in both cases, (c^2+2)/(32 pi r_0^2) and (2c^2+4)/(32 pi r_0^2): the divergent Phi'' term cancels against the b' term. The same script reproduces Lobo eq (31) exactly for finite Phi'. So R4d stands, and the attack fails.

4. Hypothesis drift. The tree adds Phi' = 0 (tolman.py:1439, 1785), which narrows the class and so is the safe direction. It drops flare-out, which V18 never uses. I grepped the warp-drive tree (excluding docket67-raw) for any conclusion that rests on flare-out = (4 pi r^3 p_r = -m), or on 'Phi' = 0 at every throat'. There is none:
- paper/CLAIMS.md:7160 and :8228 state flare-out correctly, as b'(r_0) < 1.
- detect.py, wormhole.py, definitions.py and emtension.py use Phi' = 0 as an explicitly chosen zero-tidal-force design. That class is attributed to MT, and Lobo eq (40) confirms MT [1] give it as a special class. None of them uses it as a general throat property.
So neither of the audit's NARROWED triggers fires.

5. Dependents:
- The section-1(b) non-find reason is valid: p_r(r_0) < 0 and 4 pi r_0^3 p_r = -m give m = r_0/2 > 0 at every throat, so flare-out can never coincide with negative Misner-Sharp mass.
- The W4/section-2 withdrawal rests on the computed G^r_r (V27), not on MT.

6. The two wording discrepancies are real, and both are labels rather than refutations:
- 'a throat has Phi' = 0' (tolman.py:1785, :1439).
- 'flare-out condition' attached to the throat identity (tolman.py:539-541, :2990).
Under M's rules they are recorded, not graded as WRONG.

No datum enters the result. G affects only an SI magnitude, and no sign or identity depends on it.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: run the script from a private copy, check the encoding against the published statement, and run vacuity and negation guards
verifiers.reason:
I copied the script to verify/rederive/mt.py and ran it. It reproduces exactly: 21/21, exit 0. The tree side was run read-only and matches. tolman.py --verify gives V18a = 0, V18 = 0 and V33 = -2m. --selftest prints -1.5 / -1.5 for the r_0 = 3 fixture.

ENCODING. The script tests the theorem itself, not a toy. It builds G^mu_nu from the MT metric with Phi(r) and b(r) left as arbitrary sympy Functions, and R1a/R1b match Lobo eqs (26)-(27) symbolically. I added an independent sanity check (verify/rederive/neg.py, S0): Schwarzschild gives G^mu_nu = 0, so the Einstein-tensor code is sound. P31 reproduces Lobo eq (31), p_t(r_0) = (1-b')(1+r_0 Phi')/(16 pi r_0^2), with Phi'(r_0) = k nonzero. R4a's exact identity, 4 pi r^3 p_r + m = r(r-b)Phi', is general. It carries the audit's central drift claim: at b(r_0) = r_0, V18 holds for any finite Phi'(r_0). My N3' confirms this on a concrete metric with Phi' = k != 0.

VACUITY AND NEGATION. The audit's Z2 only drops the conclusion. I negated each hypothesis in turn (neg.py, 7/7 as expected):
- Drop the throat condition b = r from Z1: SAT, including in the Lorentzian region 0 < b < r (witness r = 1, b = 7/8, Phi' = 7). The throat condition is load-bearing.
- Drop 'Phi finite', using Schwarzschild with b(r_0) = r_0: p_r(r_0) = 0, not -1/(8 pi r_0^2).
- Drop '(1-b/r)Phi' -> 0', using Phi = k ln(r - r_0) on the catenary: lim p_r(r_0) = (4k-1)/(8 pi r_0^2).
- Off the throat (r = 2 r_0, Phi' = k): the identity fails, with residual 3k r_0^2.
So the result does not pass with its hypotheses negated, and the hypotheses the audit names as needed are exactly the load-bearing ones.

MINOR OVER-STATEMENTS IN THE SCRIPT. None of these is a refutation or moves the grade.
(a) '21/21 checks' counts N1 (a test that the G spread is below 1e-3) as a check. That is information, not a test of the theorem, so the real count is 20 plus one info row.
(b) Several rows are pure arithmetic, not derivation:
- R5 hand-types p_r = -1/(72 pi) and does not read tolman.py's fixture. The tree's --selftest does read it.
- R6b, R7a, R7b and Z3 (R > 0, m = R/2, m < 0) are trivially unsat.
(c) Z1 says 'for any b'', but b' is not a variable in the encoding, so that part holds vacuously.
(d) The divergent-Phi' case is shown only by one example family (R4d), not in general. The comment there calling that Phi 'smooth in l' was not checked: near the throat Phi goes like |l|, which is a kink if mirrored across the throat.

The audit's reading of tolman.py:539-541 as a 'flare-out' mislabel is plausible, but the sentence is ambiguous. In context (tolman.py:183-187) 'flare-out' may refer to the hoped-for 'flare-out iff negative Misner-Sharp mass' equivalence. Either way it is a wording discrepancy and leaves the computed result untouched. No datum enters the result, and every check agrees with the restated source.

audits.name: In f(R), scalar-tensor, Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet and higher-curvature theories the field equations rearrange to G = 8 pi T^matter + T^effective

source.located: Primary: Sotiriou & Faraoni, 'f(R) theories of gravity', Rev. Mod. Phys. 82, 451 (2010), arXiv:0805.1726v4. It gives the metric f(R) field equations in eq (6), the effective-stress rearrangement in eqs (10)-(12) with the text on p.6, the Palatini form in eq (28), the Brans-Dicke omega=0 form in eq (55) and the energy-condition caveat on p.17. Supporting sources, all read at source: Lobo & Oliveira arXiv:0909.5539 (PRD 80, 104012, 2009), eqs (2)-(21); Bronnikov, Skvortsova & Starobinsky arXiv:1005.3262 (2010), which restates Bronnikov-Starobinsky gr-qc/0612032 (JETP Lett. 85, 1, 2007), itself NAMED-NOT-READ; Glavan & Lin arXiv:1905.03601 p.1; Guerses, Sisman & Tekin arXiv:2004.03390 p.1-4; Capozziello, Lobo & Mimoso arXiv:1407.7293, eqs (26)-(33). The tree cites no source for this result, so the audit uses the canonical review statement.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0805.1726, 0909.5539, 1005.3262, 1905.03601, 2004.03390, 1407.7293 and 2609.18475. Page text was returned and is quoted.

audits.published_statement: Sotiriou-Faraoni 0805.1726 p.6: 'it is possible to write the field equations in the form of Einstein equations with an effective stress-energy tensor composed of curvature terms moved to the right hand side. This approach is questionable in principle ... but, in practice, it has been proved to be useful in scalar-tensor gravity.' Eq (10): G_mn = kappa T_mn/f'(R) + g_mn[f - R f']/(2f') + [nabla_m nabla_n f' - g_mn box f']/f'. Eq (11): G_mn = (kappa/f')(T_mn + T^(eff)_mn), with the text 'positivity of G_eff (equivalent to the requirement that the graviton is not a ghost) imposes that f'(R) > 0'. On eq (12): 'The effective energy density derived from it is not positive-definite and none of the energy conditions holds.' p.17: energy conditions on T^(eff) are 'not very meaningful'. Scalar-tensor eq (55): G = (kappa/phi)T - gV/(2phi) + (1/phi)(nabla nabla phi - g box phi). Palatini eq (28): the source 'includes derivatives of the stress-energy tensor'. EGB: 'In D = 4 the Gauss-Bonnet invariant is a total derivative ... vanishing identically in D = 4, but not in D >= 5' (1905.03601 p.1); 'for D = 4, the H_mn tensor vanishes identically' (2004.03390 p.1). Lobo-Oliveira abstract: 'the matter threading the wormhole satisfies the energy conditions, so that it is the effective stress-energy tensor containing higher order curvature derivatives that is responsible for the null energy condition violation.' Bronnikov-Skvortsova-Starobinsky abstract: 'in cases where a wormhole is obtained, the effective gravitational constant G_eff is negative in some region of space, i.e., the graviton becomes a ghost'. Their p.6, on Lobo-Oliveira eqs (25) and (31): 'F_R is negative over some range of R for matter satisfying the weak energy condition'.
published_hypotheses: METRIC f(R) (SF eq 5-6): matter is MINIMALLY coupled to g, so nabla T = 0 (SF p.5). With a curvature-matter coupling, nabla T != 0 (1407.7293 eq 32-33).
The rearranged matter coupling is kappa/f'(R), not kappa (SF eq 11). T_eff in eq (12) is built from f, R and derivatives of f' only in that 1/f' normalisation.
f'(R) > 0 is the non-ghost / positive-G_eff condition and f'' > 0 is the Dolgov-Kawasaki condition (SF p.6, p.16). The scalar-tensor equivalence needs f'' != 0 (SF p.12).
SCALAR-TENSOR: T_eff is built from the scalar phi and V(phi), with coupling kappa/phi (SF eq 55). The non-ghost conditions are f(Phi) > 0 and l(Phi) > 0 (1005.3262 eq 2).
PALATINI f(R): the effective source contains the matter trace and its derivatives (SF eq 28).

EINSTEIN-GAUSS-BONNET: H_mn != 0 only for D >= 5 and vanishes identically in D = 4. A 4D effect needs a scalar coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term (EsGB) or the alpha/(D-4) limit, and that limit is contested (2004.03390).
The rearrangement is an interpretation, not a physical source: 'questionable in principle' (SF p.6); energy conditions on T_eff are 'somewhat misleading' (1407.7293 p.5).

Negativity under normal matter as published (Lobo-Oliveira) assumes a static spherical metric, constant redshift Phi' = 0, an anisotropic fluid and specific shape functions. Its examples have F = f' < 0.

NO-GO (Bronnikov-Starobinsky, restated in 1005.3262): if matter respects the NEC, there are no static, twice-asymptotically-flat wormholes in scalar-tensor theory with f > 0 and l > 0 everywhere, nor in F(R) with F_R > 0 everywhere.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED (coupling), overturn.py:237. The tree writes G = 8 pi T^matter + T^effective. SF eqs (10)-(11) have kappa T/f'. The 8 pi form needs kappa(1/f'-1)T moved into T^effective, so T^effective then contains the matter tensor. Check A2 shows this exactly. overturn.py:239 'T^effective is built from curvature' is therefore false in the tree's own normalisation unless f' = 1. This is a discrepancy of presentation, not of existence: the rearrangement itself is an identity (check A).

DROPPED (scalar-tensor content), overturn.py:234-239. The tree says 'built from curvature'. SF eq (55) and 1407.7293 eq (47) build it from phi, its derivatives and V(phi). In Palatini f(R) (SF eq 28) it is built from the matter trace and its derivatives. Check A3 confirms eq (55) = eq (10).

DROPPED (dimension), overturn.py:234-235. The tree lists Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet without D >= 5. In D = 4 H_mn = 0 identically: machine-checked on exact random curvature jets (check B), and stated in 1905.03601 p.1 and 2004.03390 p.1. So 4D EGB gives T^effective = 0. A 4D effect needs EsGB or the contested Glavan-Lin limit.

DROPPED (minimal matter coupling), overturn.py:235 'any higher-curvature theory'. Conservation of T^matter needs minimal coupling (SF p.5; 1407.7293 eq 32-33). As a bare identity (T_eff := G - 8 pi T) the rearrangement survives any metric theory, which is also why it carries no physical content on its own.

DROPPED (no-ghost condition), overturn.py:239-241 'An effective term can be negative where the matter term is not. If it can, L2 breaks'. SF p.6 and p.16 make f' > 0 the non-ghost condition. 1005.3262 shows that wormholes with NEC-respecting matter require G_eff < 0 somewhere. Computed here: both published WEC-respecting f(R) examples have F < 0 (check C iii); ex.(31) is exactly f = -R. In the Phi'=0 class on Lobo's eq (16), rho = F rho_eff (check D). Evidence the other way (check E): f = R - 2 Lambda with Lambda < 0 and F = 1 gives a negative effective density with no ghost, so the bare existence claim stands. The narrowing bites on the throat/wormhole use.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS, exit 0, about 15 s. (A) SF eq (6) is equivalent to eqs (10)-(12) identically on a general static spherical metric with arbitrary F(r) and f(r). (A2) In the 8 pi form, T_eff = kappa T(1/F - 1) + kappa T_eff^SF/F exactly. (A3) Eq (55) equals eq (10). (B) On exact rational curvature jets, H_mn = 0 exactly in D=4 on 3 random jets whose Gauss-Bonnet scalar is non-zero; H != 0 in D=5; trace H = -(D-4)/2 GB exactly. (C) Lobo eqs (14), (15) and (16)-(18) verified. On (16)-(18), H = 0 identically. (10)-(12) are invariant under rho -> rho - l, p -> p + l for any l(r), so (16)-(18) are fixed only by the trace eq (3) with f_R = F. ex.(31): F = -1, rho = r0^2/r^4 > 0, rho_eff + p_eff = -2r0^2/r^4 < 0, f = -R. ex.(25): F <= -1 and T = 0. (D) With Phi'=0, rho = f/2 - box F; on eq (16), rho = F rho_eff. (E) f = R - 2 Lambda gives effective density Lambda. Two source discrepancies are recorded, not treated as refutations. (1) Lobo eq (34) as extracted, at alpha = -1, gives df/dR = -5 where eq (31) requires -1; this is PDF extraction or a misprint. (2) For ex.(25), f from trace eq (3) (their eq 29, f = -RF) fails df/dR = F, with residuals 12.56, 0.685 and 0.0757 at r/r0 = 1.25, 2, 3. So their rho(16) is not the density of a metric-f(R) solution. Enforcing f = int F dR shifts rho (0.815 -> 2.278 at r = 1.25 r0) but leaves rho + p_r invariant. Neither discrepancy moves the tree's claim.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. For this result the evidence is that no missing data matters. The rearrangement is an exact identity (check A), and a negative effective term exists at the identity level (check E), so no datum the 2007-2010 authors lacked could change either. What came later was theorems and critiques that narrow the use, not data: the Bronnikov-Starobinsky no-ghost wormhole theorem, the 4D Gauss-Bonnet vanishing with its contested limit (2019-2020), and the minimal-coupling caveat (2015). Later observational bounds, such as the 2017 gravitational-wave speed mentioned in 1905.03601 p.3 and the solar-system f(R) bounds in SF sec V, limit the size of T_eff in the regimes they probe. They were not read numerically here and cannot move an identity. So the incompleteness M suspects is real, but it sits in the tree's restatement (8 pi coupling, 'built from curvature', EGB without D >= 5, no-ghost condition dropped), not in the published result.
audits.grade_evidence: The published result stands as published. The rearrangement G = (kappa/f')(T + T_eff) is an exact identity (check A). Its scalar-tensor form is SF eq (55) (check A3). An effective term can be negative: SF p.6, check E, and the re-derived Lobo-Oliveira construction (check C). The tree's use (overturn.py:234-241) holds on a smaller class than it states, for four reasons. (i) With coefficient 8 pi, T^effective contains kappa(1/f'-1)T^matter (check A2). For scalar-tensor theories it is built from phi, and for Palatini f(R) from the matter trace. (ii) EGB gives T^effective = 0 identically in D=4 (check B; 1905.03601 and 2004.03390 p.1). (iii) 'Any higher-curvature theory' needs minimal matter coupling (SF p.5; 1407.7293). (iv) The tree drops the f' > 0 no-ghost hypothesis. For the wormhole use it is load-bearing: 1005.3262 shows such wormholes need G_eff < 0 somewhere, and both published WEC-respecting f(R) examples have F < 0 (check C iii). In the Phi'=0 class on Lobo's eq (16), rho = F rho_eff (check D). The grade is not WRONG, because nothing refutes 'an effective term can be negative where matter is not'; check E is a ghost-free instance, though it is GR + Lambda. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no datum enters. The two Lobo-Oliveira discrepancies are recorded as discrepancies and do not move the grade.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restates the result with coupling kappa/f' (or says T^effective includes the matter shift), names D >= 5 or a scalar-GB coupling for EGB, names minimal coupling, and names f' > 0 as a hypothesis that the L2 break must meet or explicitly waive. To WRONG: only an error in the identity itself; check A excludes that on the static spherical class, and a general-metric check would close it everywhere. The EGB sub-clause becomes OPEN if the tree means the Glavan-Lin 4D theory, which is contested. The no-ghost narrowing lifts if someone exhibits a ghost-free higher-curvature static configuration with NEC-respecting matter and a negative Misner-Sharp mass coming from T_eff. The Lambda < 0 example (check E) is ghost-free but is GR + Lambda, so it does not count.

verifiers.reason:
I tried to overturn NARROWED in both directions and could not. The grade stands.

WHAT I CHECKED AT SOURCE (alphaXiv page text):
- Every quoted passage the audit relies on appears where it says, and the equation numbers match:
  - SF p.6: "questionable in principle"; eqs (10)-(12); f'(R) > 0 is the non-ghost condition; "none of the energy conditions holds".
  - SF p.8: eq (28), whose source "includes derivatives of the stress-energy tensor".
  - SF p.12: eq (55) and the f'' != 0 condition. SF p.17: "not very meaningful".
  - LO: abstract; eqs (10)-(18), (25), (29), (31), (34).
  - BSS: abstract; the p.6 sentence that F_R is negative in LO (25) and (31).
  - Glavan-Lin p.1: the Gauss-Bonnet tensor vanishes "identically in D = 4, but not in D >= 5". Glavan-Lin p.3 cites GW170817.
  - GST p.1: "for D = 4, the H_mn tensor vanishes identically". GST p.3: the Bianchi-identity objection.
  - CLM p.5: "somewhat misleading"; eqs (32)-(33) for non-conservation; eq (47).

INDEPENDENT CHECKS (verify/refute/mg_refute.py and mg_refute2.py):
- (1) SF eq (6) is equivalent to eq (10) as pure algebra on abstract tensor components. So the identity holds for every metric, not only the static spherical class check A tested. This closes the "general-metric" gap the audit itself flagged.
- (1b) In the tree's 8 pi form, T^eff = kappa T (1/f' - 1) + (curvature part)/f', exactly. So T^eff contains the matter tensor unless f' = 1.
- (3) LO example (31): F = -1, T = R, and f = -R exactly, which is GR with the sign of G flipped (a ghost graviton).
- (4) LO eq (34) at alpha = -1 gives df/dR = -5 where -1 is required. The misprint discrepancy is reproduced analytically.
- (2) LO example (25): f from eq (29) is numerically identical to f from the trace equation. Its residual df/dr - F dR/dr is 12.562, 0.685 and 0.0757 at r/r0 = 1.25, 2 and 3. The auditor's numbers reproduce exactly, so the inconsistency is in the paper, not in the extraction.

WHY NOT STANDS:
- The tree's literal clause "T^effective is built from curvature" is false in three cases:
  - in its own 8 pi normalisation, for any f' != 1. Check (5): f = (1+e)R is ghost-free, yet gives T^eff = -kappa e T/(1+e), which is negative wherever rho > 0. That comes purely from matter, not curvature.
  - for general scalar-tensor theories, where phi is an independent field (SF eq 55; CLM eq 47).
  - for Palatini f(R), where it is built from the matter trace (SF eq 28).
- Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet contributes T^eff = 0 identically in D = 4, which is the dimension the board works in.
- Conservation of T^matter requires minimal coupling (CLM eqs 32-33).
- Check (5) also exposes a gap the audit did not list, and it points the same way. In the 8 pi form, "an effective term can be negative" is trivially satisfiable without any negative geometric mass. A negative m(r) needs the total effective density to be negative while rho >= 0. That is a stronger condition, and in LO's class it needs F < 0.

WHY NOT WRONG:
- The rearrangement is an exact identity.
- The bare existence claim survives ghost-free: Lambda < 0 gives a negative effective density with F = 1 (check E), and so does check (5).

WHY NOT DATA-DEPENDENT OR OPEN:
- No datum enters the result, and every load-bearing source was read at source.

MINOR FAULTS (none moves the grade):
- (a) The page citation "f'' > 0 Dolgov-Kawasaki (SF p.6, p.16)" is imprecise. Dolgov-Kawasaki appears on p.16 and p.31, not p.6.
- (b) Check D (rho = F rho_eff) holds only on LO eq (16). That equation itself presumes H = 0, equivalently f = FR + 2 box F. So it describes a sub-class, not a general result for Phi' = 0. The audit does scope it "on Lobo's eq (16)".
- (c) Narrowing (iv), the no-ghost condition, bears on the wormhole and throat use. It does not bear on the tree's literal sentence, which survives ghost-free. NARROWED rests independently on (i)-(iii). The audit says this itself ("the narrowing bites on the throat/wormhole use").

VACUITY: neither of the load-bearing checks is vacuous. Check A fails when the sign of the box F term in SF eq (12) is flipped. It also fails when the coupling kappa is used with SF's T_eff. Check B fails in D=4 on all seeds under each of three mutations of the Gauss-Bonnet tensor: the t4 coefficient changed from -2 to -1, the Riem.Riem term dropped, or the GB coefficient changed from 1/4 to 1/3. B uses an exact rational Riemann tensor from a random 2-jet, so in D=4 it tests the Lovelock identity itself, not a toy. Check A uses a static spherical metric, but the identity it tests is algebraic in Ric, R, f, F and Hess F, so the restriction does not bite. The D check, rho = F rho_eff, holds by definition on Lobo's ansatz eq (16). The script itself shows that ansatz is non-unique (C ii) and is not the true density for ex.(25) (C iv). So D carries only the class it names, which is how the audit scopes it.

ENCODING DEFECT (one drift item is over-represented against the tree): Check A2 writes T_eff(8 pi form) = kappa T(1/F - 1) + kappa T_eff^SF/F. From this the audit concludes that overturn.py:239's 'T^effective is built from curvature' is false unless f' = 1. That does not follow. The split into matter and curvature parts is not unique, because T is itself fixed by SF eq (6). Substituting the field equation, I verified symbolically that the 8 pi form T_eff equals (1-F)R^m_n - (R-f)/2 delta + nabla^m nabla_n F - delta box F identically. That expression is purely geometric, since f and F are functions of R, and it contains no T. So in metric f(R) the tree's phrase 'built from curvature' is TRUE in its own 8 pi normalisation. A2 is a true identity, but its label 'contains matter unless F==1' is an artefact of the encoding. The WEAKENED (coupling) drift item and grade_evidence (i), first clause, must be withdrawn or reworded. A fair wording would be: the 8 pi form is an equivalent rewriting, with T_eff = (1-F)Ric + ..., and only its interpretation differs. For scalar-tensor theories the 8 pi form T_eff is (1-phi)G - gV/2 + nabla nabla phi - g box phi (verified). The Palatini item rests on SF eq (28) as read and is not touched by this lens.

GRADE: NARROWED still stands without the withdrawn item. The 4D EGB vanishing is solid and non-vacuous (check B). The scalar-tensor and Palatini content, the minimal-coupling caveat, and the no-ghost narrowing on the wormhole use are untouched. The check E evidence the other way, which keeps the grade from being WRONG, reproduces. So I do not mark the audit refuted, but the coupling drift item must be corrected before the audit is quoted. audits.name: SU(2)xU(1)_Y action on the Higgs doublet leaves H^dagger H invariant; -v is gauge-equivalent to +v

source.located: The classic electroweak construction (Glashow 1961, Weinberg 1967, Salam 1968; Higgs/Englert-Brout 1964) is NAMED-NOT-READ (pre-arXiv). Read through two arXiv restatements: (1) A. Maas, 'Brout-Englert-Higgs physics: From foundations to phenomenology', arXiv:1712.04721v4 (2019): eqs. (3), (4) p.2; sec. 1.3 p.2-3; sec. 3.1 eqs. (31)-(34) p.17-18 incl. footnotes 13-14; sec. 3.2 eqs. (35)-(37) p.18-19; sec. 4.7.1 p.63. (2) T. Cohen, N. Craig, X. Lu, D. Sutherland, 'Is SMEFT Enough?', arXiv:2008.08597v2 (2021): eqs. (2.7)-(2.9) p.11, sec. 4.1 eq. (4.1) p.18-19, sec. 4.2 p.25 (the CWZ linearization lemma and the O(4) fixed-point criterion).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1712.04721 (PDF pages 1,2,4-7,20-22,66,101 returned) and on 2008.08597 (PDF pages 1,4-7,11,17-19,23,25,29,30,42,44 returned). The claim is an identity about a representation of a compact Lie group on C^2, and it is also re-derived symbolically here. That re-derivation does not depend on any reading.

audits.published_statement: Maas 1712.04721 p.18-19 (sec. 3.2): 'Since the potential is, by construction, a function of gauge-invariant quantities only, so are the minima given by gauge-invariant conditions. I. e., phi^dagger phi = f^2 (35) ... In the standard model case (33), this condition takes the form X = v alpha, with v = f and alpha an arbitrary SU(2) matrix, since alpha^dagger alpha = 1. This also shows that the minimum is manifestly invariant under both, gauge transformations and custodial transformations.' p.19: 'In the standard-model case the Higgs field is in the fundamental representation of SU(2), and the only group-invariant from which an invariant potential could be built is phi^dagger phi.' p.2 (sec. 1.3): 'v, in contrast to the parameter f of the Lagrangian (3), is dependent on the gauge. In fact, it is possible to construct gauges ... in which <phi> = 0 always holds.' p.63 (sec. 4.7.1): 'The Higgs field transforms like phi -> g phi = exp(i alpha(y)) phi under a hypercharge gauge transformation.' Cohen et al. 2008.08597 p.11: H = (1/sqrt2)(phi1 + i phi2, phi3 + i phi4) <=> phi-vec = (v0 + h) n-vec (2.7); 'At zero-derivative order, there is only one O(4)-symmetric building block: |H|^2 = (1/2) phi.phi = (1/2)(v0 + h)^2 (2.8)'.
published_hypotheses: Higgs field in the fundamental (doublet) representation of SU(2)_L, with a U(1)_Y hypercharge phase exp(i alpha Y) (Maas eq. (31)-(33), p.63; Cohen et al. eq. (2.7))
a single Higgs doublet (Maas p.2 'the simplest case ... a complex doublet'; multi-doublet potentials with several minima on different orbits are treated separately, Maas p.18 and sec. 3.9)

the potential is a polynomial (renormalizable) function of gauge-invariant combinations only (Maas p.2, p.18 'For simplicity, only this polynomial case will be considered'); Cohen et al. work at zero-derivative order and assume custodial O(4) (footnote 3, p.4)
classical / tree level: 'the minima' are field configurations; at the quantum level the vev is gauge-dependent (Elitzur; Maas sec. 1.3, 3.6)
the transformation is a (global or local) gauge transformation acting on every charged field at once; a space-time-dependent element generates derivative terms (Maas eq. (31), minimal coupling)
space-time dimension >= 3 for the symmetry-breaking statements (Maas p.4, p.17)
hypothesis_drift: ADDED QUALIFIER NEEDED, NOT A REFUTATION (excite.py:181-185): 'Moving along T1, T2, T3 or Y leaves H^dagger H invariant, so no mass and no derivative-free gauge-invariant local observable changes.' Read as a gauge transformation of ALL fields, this is true by the definition of gauge invariance. If only H is moved, as the --selftest (excite.py:1578-1586) and --verify V14 (excite.py:1873-1882) do, it still holds for (a) every function of H alone, because SU(2) acts transitively on each sphere H^dag H = r^2 (S1), and (b) every mass, because the gauge-boson mass-matrix characteristic polynomial depends on H only through H^dag H (S2). It fails for a MIXED derivative-free invariant such as psi^dag H (the shape of a Yukawa L-bar H e): that changes when H alone rotates at fixed psi (CONTROL S4) and is invariant only when psi rotates with H. The tree's sentence does not say 'of H alone' or 'jointly'. Its conclusion (flat directions are inert) survives either reading, because masses are eigenvalues. This is a scope note.

UNSTATED, TREE-LEVEL (excite.py:181-185, 1087-1088 FLAT_DIRECTIONS_ARE_INERT): the tree states D19 classically and does not name that level. At the quantum level the source says the vev itself is gauge-dependent and that gauges with <phi> = 0 exist (Maas p.2, sec. 3.6, Elitzur). This does not weaken the tree's conclusion; if anything, the gauge directions are less physical.

NAMED CORRECTLY (excite.py:121-125, 1484-1489): 'in the doublet -v is gauge-equivalent to +v'. The selftest exhibits U = -I through the tree's 'Y' generator and labels it '(U = -1 in U(1)_Y)'. -I is equally the SU(2) centre element exp(i pi sigma3) (C2). No drift; recorded only because the label names one of the two subgroups that contain it.

NAMED CORRECTLY: the canonical hypotheses 'the Higgs is an SU(2) doublet with hypercharge' and 'masses depend only on H^dagger H' match the source. The second is not merely assumed: at tree level it follows from the first (S1, S2), consistent with Maas p.19 'the only group-invariant ... is phi^dagger phi'.

SINGLE DOUBLET, implicit in 'the Higgs is an SU(2) doublet' (excite.py:181-185): with two doublets, H1^dag H2 is a derivative-free invariant that is not a function of H1^dag H1, and moving one doublet relative to the other is physical. excite.py:280-288 lists 'a BSM light scalar' as unanswered, so the tree claims nothing beyond one doublet. Recorded as a named boundary, not a drift of conclusion.

DISCREPANCY IN THE RESTATING SOURCE, NOT IN THE TREE: Maas 1712.04721 footnote 13 (p.17) says 'in the standard model G = SU(2)/Z2'. Read literally, -I would act trivially and could not map H -> -H. The SM quotient is the diagonal Z6 generated by (e^{2 pi i/3}, -I, e^{2 pi i Y}), which acts trivially on every SM field (S3), while -I in SU(2) acts as -1 on H. So the element mapping H -> -H survives any quotient. Recorded as a loose footnote and not repaired. The journal version was not read, so this is not quoted as an error in it.
