I also read Kapner et al. 2007 (hep-ph/0611184) at source, which confirms the figures Lee replaced: |alpha| = 1 gives lambda <= 56 um, and R <= 44 um.

(2) The alpha convention behind the 30 um is now partly settled. Lee does not state it. Kapner (same group) states "a single extra dimension ... alpha = 8/3 and lambda = R", citing Adelberger-Heckel-Nelson 2003, and Lee cites that same reference [2] for the 30 um. So Lee's 30 um is very probably alpha = 8/3. That is READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT, not stated in Lee. If so, the alpha = 2 circle's bound lies between 30 and 38.6 um, assuming the curve is monotone. That makes the audit's use of 30 um as the worst case safe. I recomputed the shift: 42.196 -> 41.977 orders, 0.219 orders, and the selftest's rounding to 42 holds. The rederive script exits 0 with all checks passing. So moves_conclusion = No follows.

(3) value_now is right and can be upgraded. I read arXiv:2605.18212v2 (Sep 2026), which the audit had as NAMED-NOT-READ.
- The newest UW torsion result it lists is Washington 2020, i.e. Lee.
- It names "UW [7] and HUST [8]" (both 2020) as the frontier for 1 um < lambda < 1 mm.
- It gives HUST 2020's gap as 210 um and HUST 2016's as 295 um.
- It states no |alpha| = 1 crossing as a number.
So nothing after 2020 replaces Lee in this regime. The audit's refusal to call 38.6 um "still the tightest" remains properly cautious, because HUST 2020's crossing is still NAMED-NOT-READ.

(4) lacked_data answers M's hypothesis with evidence, not presumption: a wide-margin null, and no later deviation reported. It omits one thing from the source. The authors name their own data limit: "Environmental vibrations prevented us from probing separations smaller than 52 um". They also withheld their first-generation data (57 um to 2 mm) over an unidentified systematic (p3). These bear on M's question as named limits on the data, but neither touches the 38.6 um crossing, so nothing in the answer changes.

(5) Minor discrepancy, recorded and not resolved. Lee's ref [29] prints Tan et al. as PRL 124, 051310 (2020). The review and the audit give 051301. One of the two is a misprint.

Grade: no datum has moved, so DATA-DEPENDENT is not supported, and nothing is WRONG. From the data lens, NARROWED stands on the audit's dropped-|alpha|=1 finding.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE
verifiers.reason:
The audit graded this entry OPEN for one reason only: it could not read Kabat & Nomura (arXiv:2309.05759). I read that paper at source today through alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries (v2, pages 19-21). The source states the identification directly.
- Eq. 68 (p.19) reads g_AB = eta_AB + (2/Mbar5^{3/2}) h_AB, "where Mbar5 is the 5-D reduced Planck mass".
- Eq. 73 (p.20) reads "the reduced 4-D Planck mass is Mbar4 = (2 pi r)^{1/2} Mbar5^{3/2} = 2.4 x 10^18 GeV".
- Footnote 8 (p.19) gives "G4 = G5/gamma 2 pi R with G4 = 1/8 pi Mbar4^2 and G5 = 1/8 pi Mbar5^3".
- The bullets after eq. 76 (p.21) name the coupling 1/(pi r Mbar4)^2 as "built from ... the reduced 4-D Planck mass Mbar4".

What this settles:
- The tree's quotation of eqs. 68 and 72-73 (branelink.py:20-23) is accurate.
- branelink.py:146-147 ("their eq. 72-73 fix Mbar4 as the 4D reduced Planck mass") is accurate. The source says it in words and defines it through G in footnote 8.
- The audit's drift candidate ("eqs. 72-73 do not on their face define Mbar4 through G") is answered by footnote 8. It is not a drift.
- sme_coefficient (branelink.py:288-292) uses (pi r Mbar4)^2 exactly as eq. 76 does.
- Kabat & Nomura's printed 2.4e18 GeV agrees with the tree's 2.4353235e18 at the two figures they print.
- The 8 pi adverse branch in the audit's what_would_change_the_grade is therefore excluded.

The audit's numerical checks all stand, and I did not need to redo them: the definition, the CODATA 2022 G, the 2e-16 agreement and the 42-orders invariance. With the source now READ and agreeing, OPEN is no longer warranted, and the evidence supports STANDS.

Three hypotheses the tree does not name, recorded as named limitations and not as discrepancies:
- (H1) Eq. 72 is derived for a boost-like (moving) brane. Kabat & Nomura then write "We take this relation to hold in general, i.e. even for a brane that is tilt-like". For the other cases it is an assumption, not a derivation.

audits.published_statement:
Abstract (p.1): 'We present the first general model for subluminal positive-energy, spherically symmetric warp drives; construct superluminal warp-drive solutions which satisfy quantum inequalities; provide optimizations for the Alcubierre metric that decrease the negative energy requirements by two orders of magnitude ... any warp drive, including the Alcubierre drive, is a shell of regular or exotic material moving inertially with a certain velocity. Therefore, any warp drive requires propulsion. We show that a class of subluminal, spherically symmetric warp drive spacetimes, at least in principle, can be constructed based on the physical principles known to humanity today.'

Sec 3.1 (pp.9-10): eq 6 is w(r) = (1-(r/Lambda)')/(8 pi r^2). 'for purely positive energy spacetimes, Lambda(r) > 1 in the outside region D_out ... Schwarzschild'. 'any non-trivial truncated spherically symmetric warp drive must contain regions where the energy density is negative'. 'for a subluminal warp drive based on non-exotic matter, the time inside the drive can only pass more slowly than it does for a remote Minkowski observer comoving with the drive. For scale, an Earth-mass shell of 10 meter radius will slow down the rate of time by a small fraction of 4e-4.'

Sec 5.2 (p.18): 'the only type of modification to the internal spacetime that is achievable with purely positive energy for spherically symmetric warp drives is slowing down the rate of time inside the craft'. The general axisymmetric positive-energy case is left among the 'important open questions'.

Sec 5.3 (pp.18-19): 'flattening the shape by a factor of 10 would lead to proportionally smaller energy requirements'. The optimal shape f = min(r0/r_s, 1) 'reduces the energy requirement for a similarly sized Alcubierre drive by about a factor of three' (App. A.3, eq A.7: E = -(v_s^2/12) Int_{r0}^inf r_s^2 f'^2 dr_s).

Sec 5.4 (p.19): 'it is possible to construct non-trivial warp drive solutions with purely positive energy ... our work suggests a method of constructing such objects based on fully understood laws of physics.'
published_hypotheses: H1 General warp drive (sec 2.1, p.4): an asymptotically flat vacuum region D_out encloses a compact curved region D_warp of spherical topology, which encloses a flat passenger region D_in. The spacetime is stationary, with a global Killing field xi aligned with the 4-velocity of the inner boundary.

H2 Positive-energy class (sec 3.1, p.9): spherical symmetry, meaning an SO(3) whose orbits are orthogonal to xi. B-M state this is possible 'only for class I and IV spacetimes, i.e., subluminal warp drives'.

H3 'Positive energy' means the energy density w in the comoving/Eulerian frame (eq 6). There is no evaluation for all timelike observers and no NEC/DEC/SEC check on the pages read. SSV 2105.03079 p.11 says the Eulerian density 'is the only quantity Bobrick-Martire explicitly calculate'.

H4 The matter in D_warp is an isotropic, barotropic fluid, rho = rho(P), with P = 0 at the inner and outer boundaries (p.10, eqs 8-9). This is the premise of N(r_in) = N(r_out), and so of 'time can only pass more slowly'.
H5 In the spherical case, the only interior modification purely positive energy can produce is slower interior time (p.18). Positive-energy axisymmetric metrics are left open (p.18).
H6 'Physical' is qualified: 'at least in principle' (abstract) and 'our work suggests' (p.19). No explicit shell with every energy condition verified is constructed.

H7 The optimisations (sec 5.3, A.3) act on the Alcubierre metric, whose Eulerian energy stays negative-definite. The factor ~3 is 'for a similarly sized Alcubierre drive' and was found 'numerically'; the comparison parameters are not stated on the pages read. The flattening law is E -> E/alpha_X (p.14); its derivation on pp.11-13 was NOT READ.
H8 Superluminal drives 'may always violate weak energy conditions', 'an established fact (Olum 1998, Visser et al. 2000)'. B-M say their own argument for this is not a strict proof (p.18).

At source, B-M compute only the Eulerian density (H3; SSV p.11 READ; BBV Error 28 READ) and never claim NEC/DEC/SEC. B-M's positive-energy class is subluminal by construction (H2). WARP-DRIVE.md:335-336 already records that B-M 'check only Eulerian observers', which agrees with the source.

SOURCE UNDERSTATED at warpfolder.py:143-150. M's rule forbids over-representation in either direction, and this one runs against the source. The rebuttal of the folder's 'positive-energy physical shells' quotes WARP-DRIVE.md:213 ('none of that makes the energy positive'). audits.published_statement: Carroll gr-qc/9712019 p.81: 'R_{rho sigma mu nu} = -R_{sigma rho mu nu} allows us to write this result as nabla_[lambda R_rho sigma] mu nu = 0 . (3.88) This is known as the Bianchi identity. (Notice that for a general connection there would be additional terms involving the torsion tensor.) ... An especially useful form of the Bianchi identity comes from contracting twice on (3.87): 0 = g^{nu sigma} g^{mu lambda}(nabla_lambda R_{rho sigma mu nu} + nabla_rho R_{sigma lambda mu nu} + nabla_sigma R_{lambda rho mu nu}) = nabla^mu R_{rho mu} - nabla_rho R + nabla^nu R_{rho nu} , (3.93) or nabla^mu R_{rho mu} = (1/2) nabla_rho R . (3.94) (Notice that, unlike the partial derivative, it makes sense to raise an index on the covariant derivative, due to metric compatibility.) If we define the Einstein tensor as G_{mu nu} = R_{mu nu} - (1/2) R g_{mu nu} , (3.95) then we see that the twice-contracted Bianchi identity (3.94) is equivalent to nabla^mu G_{mu nu} = 0 . (3.96)'. p.117: '... simply take the metric of your choice, compute the Einstein tensor G_{mu nu} for this metric, and then demand that T_{mu nu} be equal to G_{mu nu}. The metric is smooth enough for nabla R to exist classically: third derivatives of g enter nabla G, so C^3 is sufficient. The source leaves this implicit.
No field equation is assumed for (3.96) itself. The conservation consequence needs G = 8 pi G T, optionally with -Lambda g, which metric compatibility conserves on its own.
What comes out is LOCAL covariant conservation nabla_mu T^{mu nu} = 0 (4.23), not an integral energy law in general. Carroll p.37 notes that gravitational energy has no sensible local tensor.

verifiers.reason:
The NARROWED grade survives in both directions. I read the source myself this time: one alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries call on gr-qc/9712019v1 returned pdf pages 57, 65-69, 80, 82-88 and 100.

(1) THE SOURCE PAGE THE AUDIT COULD NOT READ supports the grade. On printed p.80 (pdf 87), Carroll says, verbatim: "In addition to the algebraic symmetries of the Riemann tensor (which constrain the number of independent components at any point), there is a differential identity which it obeys (which constrains its relative values at different points)". He then derives (3.87) in Riemann normal coordinates from third derivatives of g, using the Christoffel form. At source, the identity is therefore distinct from the algebraic symmetries and needs third derivatives of the metric. permute.py:103-106 says it "holds for every metric, differentiable ... it follows from the symmetries of the Riemann tensor alone". As stated, that extends the result to every field with the algebraic Riemann symmetries, a strictly larger class, and drops the differential and C^3 hypotheses. That matches the rubric for NARROWED: "holds on a smaller class than the tree uses, or a hypothesis the tree drops". It is not WRONG. The identity itself is true, and the misstatement is a discrepancy in wording, which the audit records correctly. Printed p.81 (pdf 88), where the torsion caveat sits, and the p.117/118 "automatically conserved" text both match the audit's quotes word for word.

(2) THE COMPUTATIONS REPRODUCE, and my own independent re-derivation agrees. The auditor's script with --fast gives 25/25. I also wrote and ran verify/refute/cbi_indep.py, which uses a different method:
- A generic 4D polynomial metric with all 10 components carrying random cubic coefficients, Levi-Civita connection, exact rational degree-3 jets at the origin.
- nabla_mu G^{mu nu}(0) = [0,0,0,0] exactly.
- The check is not vacuous: G^{00}(0) = -4302195687/7702870756, and the divergence with partial derivatives only (connection terms dropped) is non-zero in all four components.
- Control: R_abcd = phi(eta_ac eta_bd - eta_ad eta_bc) has every algebraic symmetry. It gives G_ab = -3 phi eta_ab, and div_b G^b_0 = -3 d_0 phi, which is non-zero. So B1's counterexample to "symmetries alone" stands.

(3) THE GRADE DOES NOT OVERSTATE AGAINST THE TREE. The audit says explicitly that no owner uses the identity outside its true class: every G the owners build is the Christoffel curvature of a smooth metric. O5, specthm R7, specthm W and permute's EXACT verdict are left untouched. The B3 finding is recorded as a discrepancy in the tree's evidence, not as an error in the result, and it is right. continuity_residual is identically zero on phase space, the step series reproduces at 6.03e-16 / 5.68e-16 / 5.88e-16, and the positive control catches a wrong acceleration law.

(4) TWO CORRECTIONS, neither of which moves the grade.
(a) The 'ADDED off-shell conservation' drift should not carry weight. hpscentre.py:157-160 does not attribute conservation "for arbitrary f, r" to the Bianchi identity. It gives no justification at all. Bianchi is named only at hpscentre.py:1235 (div G = 0 on the metric) and :1401 (the thth step), and both are within the true class: C1 and C2 reproduce, and the r' != 0 caveat is correct. The off-shell premise is a separate external result, conservation of the renormalised <T> in an arbitrary background, the effective-action / Wald-axiom property. It came in through the canonical merge. It is fair to record it as a named hypothesis, but it is not drift of this theorem. The grade rests on permute.py:103-106 alone, and that is enough.
(b) The audit's source note "printed p.80 (pdf 87) not quoted" can now be upgraded to READ via alphaXiv, quoted above. Carroll p.93 (pdf 100) also gives the Cartan-form Bianchi identity (3.141) for general connections. With torsion, the component form gains torsion terms, which is consistent with the p.81 caveat and with B2.

audits.published_statement: NOT READ AT SOURCE this pass, so nothing is quoted. Re-derived here with sympy (10/10 PASS): (i) Exact, nonlinear case. Take a static, straight string core with T^t_t = T^z_z, which is boost invariance along the axis (Psi' = 0 in the tree's metric), and define mu = INT u dA = 2 pi INT_0^R u W dr. The exterior is a flat cone with deficit angle exactly 8 pi G mu, for either sign of mu. Checked on the uniform cores W = r0 sin(r/r0) with u = +1/(8 pi r0^2), and W = r0 sinh(r/r0) with u = -1/(8 pi r0^2). The cone closes at G mu = 1/4. (ii) Linearised case with general stress (energy per length mu, tension tau): deficit = 4 pi G (mu + tau). This equals 8 pi G mu only when tau = mu.
published_hypotheses: NOT READ AT SOURCE. These are the hypotheses under which the formula was re-derived here.
H1: the string is static, straight and infinite (cylindrical symmetry, translation invariance along z).
H2: tension equals energy per unit length, T^z_z = T^t_t (boost invariance along the string). 'Deficit = 8 pi G mu' needs this. Without it the linear deficit is 4 pi G (mu + tau).

H3: mu is the proper integral INT u dA over a smooth core, and the thin limit is taken of smooth sources. A conical singularity is not itself a distributional source (Geroch-Traschen 1987, NAMED-NOT-READ).
H4: the exterior is vacuum. The formula is exact beyond linear order for boost-invariant cores (re-derived B+/B-). The general-stress formula is weak-field only (re-derived D).
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H2 (tension = energy density). axial.py:130-135 says 'its deficit is 8 pi G mu' and 'AN ANGLE EXCESS IS THE DEFICIT OF A NEGATIVE mu' with no condition, for 'ordinary matter'. Re-derived D/E: a thin string with tension tau != mu has deficit 4 pi G (mu + tau). So mu = +0.01, tau = -0.02 (axial pressure 2 mu, larger than mu) gives an angle EXCESS (deficit -pi/25) with POSITIVE mu. It satisfies the NEC along z (rho + p_z = 0.03 > 0) and violates the DEC (p_z > rho). Outside H2 the sentence as written is false: an excess needs either mu < 0 or an axial pressure larger than mu.

UNSTATED tree hypothesis that puts H2 back. In axial.py:182-183, WITH_CONICAL_DEFECT drops the axis boundary term [W Psi']_{r=0}, which means it assumes W Psi' -> 0 at the axis. axial.py:186-187 HYPOTHESES lists 'regular axis W(0)=0, W'(0)=1' and 'W Psi' -> 0' at infinity only. audits.published_statement: Schwarzschild 1916 interior (physics/9912033): inside a homogeneous incompressible sphere, eq.(35) ds^2 = ((3 cos chi_a - cos chi)/2)^2 dt^2 - (3/kappa rho0)[dchi^2 + sin^2 chi dOmega^2], with rho0 + p = rho0 2 cos chi_a/(3 cos chi_a - cos chi) (eq.30). The 'radius measured outside' is P_o = sqrt(3/kappa rho0) sin chi_a, and eq.(40) gives alpha/P_o = sin^2 chi_a, alpha = (kappa rho0/3) P_o^3. 'At the center of the sphere velocity of light and pressure become infinite when cos chi_a = 1/3 ... Hence there is a limit to the concentration, above which a sphere of incompressible fluid can not exist.' 'a sphere of given gravitational mass alpha/2k^2 can not have a radius measured from outside smaller than: P_o = alpha. For a sphere of incompressible fluid the limit will be 9/8 alpha. (For the Sun alpha is equal to 3 km, for a mass of 1 gram is equal to 1.5 . 10^-28 cm.)' Hayward (gr-qc/9408002), with E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)): 'Proposition 1: trapping. A metric sphere is trapped if and only if E > r/2, marginal if and only if E = r/2, and untrapped if and only if E < r/2. Proof. By definition.' The gloss adds that 'the ratio E/r controls the formation of black and white holes, and trapped spheres generally'. The textbook form the tree uses: a uniform ball of areal radius l has M = u (4/3) pi l^3/c^2 and is (marginally) trapped iff 2GM/c^2 >= l.
published_hypotheses: classical GR, Einstein's field equations with no cosmological constant (1916: kappa = 8 pi k^2)

1916 interior: STATIC equilibrium, isotropic perfect fluid of CONSTANT density rho0 ('incompressible'), regular centre with finite positive central pressure, p = 0 and C^1 matching at the surface
the radius in the criterion is the AREAL radius ('radius measured from outside'), not the proper radius
the mass in the criterion is the gravitational (Schwarzschild / Misner-Sharp) mass alpha/2k^2, not the 'substantial mass' over proper volume (eq.41, 43: the two differ)
Hayward Prop.1 is about TRAPPING of a metric sphere, future OR past, not about black holes: a black hole is a future outer trapping horizon, a white hole a past one

audits.lacked_data: In 1916 Schwarzschild had the field equations and the Newtonian limit. Later work sharpens it two ways, both computed here: (i) it is a TRAPPING criterion, a trapped sphere can be past-trapped (a white hole, R5), and black-hole formation needs Penrose plus censorship; this narrows 'is a black hole' to 'is trapped, hence not static' (R4), which is all the verdict needs; (ii) the stricter static bound 8/9 was already in the 1916 paper and raises the tree's ratio to 3 pi^2/4 (R6d). audits.published_statement: FO p.10, verbatim: 'Theorem 4.2. Let omega_2^0 be the two-point function of a reference Hadamard state for the non-minimally coupled scalar field with coupling constant xi in [0, 1/4], defined on a globally hyperbolic spacetime with smooth metric. Furthermore, let gamma be a time-like geodesic parametrised in proper time tau and let f in D(R, R). On the set of Hadamard states, we then find (rho_quant o gamma)(f^2) >= -Q_xi(f), (44) where Q_xi(f) = Qt_A^xi(f) 1 + xi (:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_B[f]) + xi (:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_C^xi[f]), (45) with Qt_A^xi(f) = int_0^oo dalpha/pi [ phi*(rho1^ omega_2^0)(f_alpha, f_alpha) + 2 xi alpha^2 phi* omega_2^0 (f_alpha, f_alpha) ], (46) and Q_B(f) and Q_C^xi(f) are functions in D(R, R) given by Q_B[f](tau) = 2 (d_tau f(tau))^2, (47) Q_C^xi[f](tau) = f(tau)^2 ( R_mn gamma^m gamma^n - (1/2)(1 - 4 xi) R )(tau). (48) Furthermore Qt_A^xi(f) and Q_B[f] are non-negative. This result follows from the previous discussion by discarding manifestly positive terms. We remark that Qt_A^xi(f) depends on the reference state and that for xi = 0, we recover results known for minimal coupling [5]. Moreover, Q_C^xi(f) vanishes if the region of interest is Ricci-flat.' rho_quant is normal ordered: <G_quant>_Psi = [sum D_i :omega_2^Psi:]_c, :omega_2^Psi: = omega_2^Psi - omega_2^0 (eq. 6).

audits.lacked_data: Theorem 4.2 has NO empirical input. It is derived from the field equation, the Hadamard condition and the positive-type property of Fewster 2000's point-split operator, and its only parameters are xi (chosen) and an arbitrary geometry, so there is no measured datum the authors could have lacked. Evidence FOR the theorem as published: 22/22 checks here, covering (7)=(8), (9)=(10)-(14), the exact-derivative smearing step producing (47)-(48), the z3 range proof, an independent MTW derivation of (48) on a curved metric, and the Minkowski reduction to Fewster-Eveson. Two later papers by overlapping authors (1809.05047, 2019; 2309.10848, 2023) re-use and cite the result without correcting it, and the only printed correction to FO (1809.05047 fn.4, beta^{2-n}) is in the Sec.5 KMS example, with 'final results correct'. Evidence of INCOMPLETENESS, not error: (i) xi in [0,1/4] is a limit of the proof, and this stage computed that it is also sharp for inequalities of form (44)-(45), so for xi > 1/4 the form fails (check G); (ii) FFKP 2023 obtained a null-contracted bound for all xi, which is a different quantity; (iii) 1809.05047 extended the method to accelerated curves for the effective energy density. FO's successors supply none of these. M's hypothesis is therefore not supported for this result: it is incomplete in named ways (range, geodesic, difference type), not inaccurate.

audits.published_statement:
Kontou-Sanders (2020), eq.(17), verbatim: 'For a null congruence with tangent field k^a, parametrized by affine parameter lambda, the expansion theta = nabla_a k^a satisfies dtheta/dlambda = -R_ab k^a k^b - sigma_ab sigma^ab + omega_ab omega^ab - theta^2/(n-2)', where 'n is the spacetime dimension, sigma_ab is the shear tensor and omega the vorticity'. They add: 'Unless otherwise noted, we will consider irrotational congruences, meaning that the rotation tensor vanishes'; the equation 'is derived from the trace of the geodesic deviation equation'; 'For theories that obey Einstein's equation we may rewrite these energy conditions by eliminating the stress tensor in favour of the Ricci curvature tensor'.

Wall (2010), eq.(7): '-dtheta/dlambda = (1/2) theta^2 + sigma_ab sigma^ab + 8 pi G T_ab k^a k^b'. Footnote 14: 'the classical background Raychaudhuri Eq. (7) can take over ... to show the existence of the conjugate point'. Abstract: the positivity theorems 'fail once the linearized graviton field is quantized, because then the renormalized shear squared term in the Raychaudhuri equation can be negative'.

Gao-Wald (2000), eqs.(11)-(13), re-quoted: d^2A/dlambda^2 = -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu, with A|p = 0 and dA/dlambda|p = delta; G = sqrt(det A); 'the Raychaudhuri equation yields G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b]'. Conjugate points are the zeros of G.

The tree's u'' = -q u, q = 4 pi T_kk, u(0) = 0 is this equation with sigma = omega = 0, n = 4 and R_kk = 8 pi T_kk (G = c = 1).

H2 Irrotational (omega_ab = 0). Otherwise +omega^2 enters with a DEFOCUSING sign (eq.17). This is automatic for the congruence from a point (A|p = 0): measured twist |B01 - B10| <= 3.2e-12 (S4).
H3 Spacetime dimension n. The coefficient is 1/(n-2), so the tree's 1/2, and hence its 4 pi, hold at n = 4 only (S1, S2: q = 8 pi T_kk/(n-2)).
H4 Einstein's equation (classical GR), used to replace R_kk by 8 pi G T_kk / c^4. Lambda and the trace term drop because g_kk = 0 (S2, exact in n = 4, 5, 6).
H5 sigma_ab sigma^ab >= 0. This is true classically, as a sum of squares of a real spatial tensor. Wall 0910.5751: the RENORMALISED shear-squared can be negative once gravitons are quantised.

H6 Shear is sourced by the Weyl tensor through the Jacobi (Sachs) equation. Setting sigma = 0 is EXACT only where the Weyl (traceless tidal) part vanishes along the ray (S3a). H7 Point initial data u(0) = 0, u'(0) = 1, i.e. conjugate points to a point. A surface-orthogonal congruence has focal-point data u(0) = 1, u'(0) = theta_0/2 instead.

audits.published_statement: NOT READ AT SOURCE. What follows is from web-search summaries of the abstracts, not quotations from the papers. [1309.6303] Flat cosmological spacetimes with a massive, conformally coupled scalar field. Initial conditions at finite time give a state with finite stress-tensor expectation values. The paper proves existence and uniqueness of local solutions, for the metric and the matter field together. Local solutions extend until the scale factor becomes singular or the Hubble function reaches a critical value H_c = 180 pi/G. [1001.0864] Local (and, per one summary, global) existence for a massive conformally coupled scalar on flat FLRW, solving for the state and the Hubble function together in an integral-functional equation. [2007.14665] Existence and uniqueness on flat FLRW for a massive scalar with arbitrary coupling xi. The problem is recast as a fixed point on a Banach space, giving short-time existence and uniqueness by the Banach fixed point theorem. [1809.03812] Existence in cosmological spacetimes without the conformal-coupling restriction and with the full renormalisation freedom, treated as an infinite-dimensional dynamical system.

The Lanczos/Israel junction the model rests on is audited separately (israel-lanczos-poisson-visser-thin-shell, STANDS). Read at source text: (i) N. Dadhich, arXiv:2504.00064v2 p.7, restating the Einstein-Vlasov numerics of Ames, Andreasson & Logg (arXiv:1603.05404, 1803.11224; NAMED-NOT-READ): 'as the limiting compactness M/R -> 4/9 is approached, the shell becomes infinitely thin ... in the limit, p_r/rho -> 0 and 2p_t/rho -> 1 ... particle velocity attains the value, v^2 = 8/9. (read, PSP sec. X, restating LeMaitre-Poisson 2019) A barotropic shell is radially stable in the Newtonian limit iff Gamma >= 3/2. This is a statement about a fluid. The kinetic shell obeys it because its equation of state is barotropic along the L-conserving sequence (K4).
hypothesis_drift: The single-speed hypothesis is unstated, and the conclusion is widened to the whole class. wall.py:98-99 says 'counter-rotating matter clears the threshold only for x < 0.46898'. That number holds only when every particle shares one speed (wall.py:79 'sigma = n mu gamma'; the canonical entry lists only 'isotropic tangential directions'). Computed in K7a: the thin limit of an Einstein cluster has the same Lanczos statics (checked at x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 to 2e-6), and every particle in it sits on its own circular geodesic. Its speeds spread over v^2 in [0, x/(2(1-x))]. With each particle conserving its own L, its crossover is x = 0.447387, not 0.468977, and its margin at x = 0.3 is 1.133151, not 1.144558. Two-speed mixtures with the same statics give 0.445357 and 0.430510 (K7b). Mixtures with most rest mass at rest fall below 0.1 (K7c), but those are not realizable as particles that each hold their own orbit. What the stated class drops: the monoenergetic-|L| hypothesis.

The '4/3 exactly as x -> 0' limit (wall.py:88, 98-99, 430-431, 606-611) is 2/(3/2): the Newtonian Gamma = 2 of a 2D gas against the Gamma = 3/2 threshold (PSP sec. X, restating LeMaitre-Poisson). It needs non-relativistic particle speeds, and a single speed guarantees that (v^2 ~ x/4). For any fixed speed distribution the limit still holds (K7a; K7c at x = 1e-6). How fast the margin approaches it depends on the distribution: with rest fraction 0.999 the margin is 1.259 at x = 1e-3 and 0.939 at x = 1/6.

Radial perturbations only. The model's beta^2 is defined by a spherically symmetric perturbation (wall.py:81). wall.py:119-128 imports the l >= 2 instability of Pitre-Schneider-Poisson and calls their configuration 'LE'S STATIC ANCHOR EXACTLY'. But PSP's shell is a perfect fluid (2604.05980v1, cached line 459). Nothing read here establishes that the l >= 2 instability carries over to a collisionless counter-rotating shell. That fluid-to-kinetic transfer at wall.py:124-125 is added without being stated. It sits next to this key rather than inside it.

A labelling discrepancy, cross-referenced to audit einstein-vlasov-limit-2-3. wall.py:29 and wall.py:245 call x = 2/3 the 'Einstein-Vlasov limit'. The file's own 'counter-rotating (Einstein-Vlasov) shell' (wall.py:77) expires at 8/9 (wall.py:83). K2 confirms 8/9 for the single-speed model. The sibling audit showed 2/3 is where the outermost particle of the thin-limit cluster reaches v = 1. This is a label, not an arithmetic error.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. The model uses no measured datum. Every quantity is a closed-form function of the compactness x, and every one was re-derived exactly (K1-K6). That includes the equation-of-motion test that never uses beta^2_crit and reproduces the crossover to 1e-9. So there is no missing measurement that could move this result, which is evidence against M's hypothesis for this entry. What the model does leave out is a microstate input: how the particles' speeds are distributed. The tree gives every particle one speed. The natural alternative with the same statics is the thin limit of an Einstein cluster, where each particle sits on its own circular geodesic. It gives a crossover of 0.447387 instead of 0.468977 (4.6% lower) and a margin of 1.133 instead of 1.145 at x = 0.3. That input moves the number but none of the conclusions the tree draws from it. x = 0.3 stays stable, x = 2/3 and x = 4/5 stay unstable, and the x -> 0 limit stays 4/3. designpoint.py:160-161 checks that 1/6 is below the crossover, and that still holds (1/6 < 0.447). Only unrealizable rest-dominated mixtures break these conclusions, and they are recorded as unrealizable, not as refutations.
audits.grade_evidence: Every closed-form statement re-derives exactly (34 of 34 checks pass). The crossover is (17 - sqrt33)/24, and the equation-of-motion test, which does not use beta^2_crit, finds the same value. The table rows, the 1.144557648 margin, the 4/3 limit and the 8/9 expiry are all reproduced, and the Israel conservation law holds identically. No datum enters, so none can move. The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS for one computed reason. wall.py:98-99 states the result for 'counter-rotating matter' as a class, but 0.46898 holds only under the unstated single-speed hypothesis. The thin-limit Einstein cluster, which has the same statics and whose particles each hold their own orbit, gives 0.447387 (K7a). The tree's qualitative conclusions hold in that model too. The provenance claim is OPEN.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: Two routes lead to STANDS. One is to restate wall.py:98-99 for a single-speed shell, with x_c = (17 - sqrt33)/24. The other is to show that a static thin Einstein-Vlasov shell must have a single speed, which would remove the K7 alternative. The route to WRONG is a published kinetic-shell stability analysis showing that the L-conserving radial response is not barotropic. K4 is evidence against that. The provenance sub-claim leaves OPEN once a literature search can be run; one was blocked here.

audits.published_statement: PDG 2026 gives m_u = 2.16 +- 0.07 MeV, m_d = 4.70 +- 0.07 MeV, mbar = 3.49 +- 0.07 MeV and m_u/m_d = 0.462 +- 0.020. The 2024 and 2025 editions give the same values. PDG 2019-2023 gave m_u = 2.16 (+0.49/-0.26) and m_d = 4.67 (+0.48/-0.17). PDG header text (2026), verbatim: 'The u-, d-, and s-quark masses are estimates of so-called ``current-quark masses,'' in a mass- independent subtraction scheme such as MSbar. The ratios mass(u)/mass(d) and mass(s)/mass(d) are extracted from pion and kaon masses using chiral symmetry. The estimates of d and u masses are not without controversy ... there are even suggestions that the u quark could be essentially massless. ... We have normalized the MSbar masses at a renormalization scale of mu = 2 GeV. Results quoted in the literature at mu = 1 GeV have been rescaled by dividing by 1.35.' PDG publishes no value for 2m_u + m_d. That sum is the tree's own arithmetic on PDG's two entries.
published_hypotheses: Current-quark masses in a mass-independent subtraction scheme (MS-bar), per the PDG text
Renormalisation scale mu = 2 GeV, with results quoted at 1 GeV rescaled by 1/1.35, per the PDG text
m_u/m_d and m_s/m_d taken from pion and kaon masses via chiral symmetry

'Our Evaluation' is determined in part from Figures 2-3 of the RPP Quark-masses review, so it is not a pure weighted average. The computed averages are m_u 2.16+-0.04 (scale factor 1.157) and m_d 4.70+-0.04
Inputs are lattice QCD (n_f = 2+1 and 2+1+1, some with QED) and sum rules
PDG's caveat: the u and d masses are 'not without controversy', and m_u may be 'essentially massless'

audits.lacked_data: Tested for this result, and the evidence is that the missing data does not change the conclusion. The authors of the value the tree uses (RPP 2019-2023) did lack later data. audits.name: CMB temperature scales as T proportional to 1/a (adiabatic blackbody redshifting), so T_rec/T_0 = 1+z

source.located: The law is a textbook result with no single originating paper. Its modern statement and tests: Chluba 2014, MNRAS 443, 1881, arXiv:1405.1277; Avgoustidis et al. 2016, PRD 93, 043521, arXiv:1511.04335; Riechers et al. 2022, Nature 602, 58, arXiv:2202.00693. The two data the tree uses: T_0 from Fixsen 2009, ApJ 707, 916, arXiv:0911.1955; z* = 1089.92 from Planck 2018 VI, arXiv:1807.06209.
source.via: Read as page text: Planck 2018 VI, from the cached full text scratchpad/d67/src/casmag/all/1807.06209v4.txt (md5 520b9b5e0258d40eddee9e463c1577c3). Line 1045 reads 'We take T0 = 2.7255K (Fixsen 2009), with the +/-0.0006K error having negligible impact on results'. Lines 1193-1217 hold the Table 2 caption: 'Parameter 68 % intervals for the base-LCDM model ... The middle group lists derived parameters'. Lines 1333-1336 hold the z* row, one value per data combination: 1090.30, 1089.57, 1087.8, 1089.95, 1089.92+/-0.25 (TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing) and 1089.80. I did not find Planck's definition of z* in the cached text, so it is not quoted. Not read as page text: every alphaXiv call in this stage (answer_pdf_queries on 0911.1955, 1807.06209, 1112.1862 and 1405.1277; get_paper_content; discover_papers) returned 'assistant quota exceeded'. ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org, academic.oup.com and pith.science are EGRESS_BLOCKED. The following are search-engine summaries from WebSearch, which are weaker than page text. Fixsen 2009: T_0 = 2.72548+/-0.00057 K. Chluba 2014 abstract: T_CMB is proportional to (1+z); adiabatic photon production or anisotropy could modify this, but in practice it would instead produce a spectral distortion that FIRAS limits. Avgoustidis 2016: beta = (7.6+/-8.0)e-3. Riechers 2022: T(z=6.34) = 16.4-30.2 K. Ivanov, Ali-Haimoud and Lesgourgues 2020 (2005.10656): CMB anisotropies alone constrain T_0 only weakly. 2607.23535: 63 measurements over 0<=z<=6.34. The law itself is re-derived from first principles here, so the grade does not depend on these summaries.

audits.published_statement: The law, from a search-engine summary of the Chluba 2014 abstract: 'In the expanding Universe, the average temperature of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) is expected to depend like T_CMB proportional to (1+z) on redshift z. Adiabatic photon production (or destruction) or deviations from isotropy and homogeneity could modify this scaling.' The data, read at page text in Planck 2018 VI: 'We take T0 = 2.7255K (Fixsen 2009)' (line 1045), and z* = 1089.92+/-0.25 as a DERIVED parameter of the base-LCDM fit to TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing (Table 2). Re-derived here: a Planck occupation that is free-streaming in FLRW stays exactly a Planck occupation with T = T_e a_e/a.
published_hypotheses: An FLRW background, with photon momentum p proportional to 1/a along null geodesics
Photons are collisionless after decoupling, so the occupation number is conserved along each ray (Liouville)

No photon production or destruction and no energy injection after thermalisation. If there were, the result would be a mu or y spectral distortion rather than a rescaled T (Chluba 2014, search summary).
The spectrum was a blackbody when set, as the FIRAS measurement of T_0 assumes and fits
The value z* = 1089.92 depends on the base-LCDM model with T_0 fixed at 2.7255 K; it is a derived parameter, not a direct measurement
Reading the result as a (cosmic scale)/(atomic scale) ratio needs alpha, m_e and hbar to be constant since z*
hypothesis_drift: ADDED at permute.py:239 ('Measured independently of any model of a(t)') and permute.py:66-68 ('from the CMB temperature alone'). permute.py:234-240 computes T_rec = T_0(1+z) and then divides by T_0, so the ratio is identically 1+z for any T_0. sympy gives d/dT_0 = 0, and the live near-check at permute.py:428-429 still passes with T_0 = 1e6 K. The only input, z*, is a base-LCDM derived parameter with T_0 fixed (Planck 2018 VI, lines 1045 and 1193-1217).

ADDED at obstruct.py:278 ('read off T_rec/T_0'): the same drift, carried into the EXPANSION-IS-A-RELABELLING row. That row's independent ground, theta = 3H_0 != 0 (obstruct.py:273-276), does not use this result.
DROPPED at permute.py:179 ('Z_REC = 1089.92  # Planck 2018'): the comment does not say the value is derived from base LCDM. Across Planck's six Table 2 columns, z* runs from 1087.8 to 1090.30.
DROPPED at permute.py:62-66 and 243-245 (bohr_radius_contains_a hard-codes False): the assumption that alpha, m_e and hbar are constant since z* is never named as a hypothesis.
DROPPED: direct T_CMB(z) measurements reach only 0<=z<=6.34 (search summaries). At z*, the scaling rests on the theorem plus the LCDM fit, not on measurement.

LABEL DISCREPANCY, not a refutation: the constant is named Z_REC and the prose says 'recombination' (permute.py:67-70, obstruct.py:278), but the value is z*, the last-scattering redshift (z_drag = 1059.94 is a separate row). By the Saha equation, hydrogen is half-ionised at 3762 K (z = 1379); at 2973.3 K the ionised fraction is 3.2e-3.
No drift on the core law: the canonical entry names exactly the published and re-derived hypotheses (free-streaming FLRW photons, no injection).

rederivation.outcome: All 19 checks pass, exit 0. A1: a free-streaming Planck occupation equals Planck with T = T_e a_e/a, identically. A2 and A3: the Bose integrals, computed to 40 digits, give n ~ a^-3 and rho ~ a^-4. A4: a mu-distortion is not absorbed into T. B1 and B2: adiabatic w = 1/3 forces rho ~ a^-4. C1-C5: the tree's ratio is a tautology (d/dT_0 = 0), and the live permute call passes for T_0 from 1e-3 K to 1e6 K. D1: 2.7255 x 1090.92 = 2973.30246 K, matching the tree. D3: the spread of z* across Planck columns is 2.3e-3 of 1+z*. E1: Saha half-ionisation at 3762 K. F: extrapolating beta gives a band of 0.897 to 1.003.

63 T_CMB(z) measurements over 0<=z<=6.34 constrain violations to the percent level

audits.lacked_data: The law predates every T(z) measurement, so its authors lacked high-redshift temperatures and FIRAS-precision spectra. Both have since arrived and move nothing. Tests over 0<=z<=6.34 are consistent with the law (beta consistent with 0; T(6.34) as expected), and distortion limits close the adiabatic-injection loophole. All of these come from search-engine summaries. Nothing found contradicts the law, and no later data reach z*. What the tree lacks is a status point, not a physics datum: it treats z* as model-free, but z* is derived from base LCDM with T_0 fixed (read in Planck 2018 VI). Adding that fact leaves the conclusion unchanged, since 1+z* lies between 1088.8 and 1091.3 in every Planck column. M's hypothesis is not supported for this result.
audits.grade_evidence: The law holds. It is re-derived symbolically (A1, B1, B2) under exactly the hypotheses the tree names, and search summaries corroborate it up to z = 6.34. The grade is NARROWED because the tree claims more: permute.py:66-68 and 239 and obstruct.py:278 say the ratio is 'measured independently of any model of a(t)'. Shown here: the code's ratio is identically 1+z for every T_0, and the near-check passes even at T_0 = 1e6 K. Its one input, z* = 1089.92, is a base-LCDM derived parameter with T_0 fixed (Planck 2018 VI, lines 1045 and 1193-1217, read as page text). The tree also leaves unnamed the assumption of constant atomic constants and the z<=6.34 limit of direct tests. audits.lacked_data: Hawking & Ellis (1973) stated a taxonomy. It is definitional, uses no data, and re-derives here (C1). What they and the 1970s catalogue lacked was semiclassical data: renormalized quantum stress tensors on black-hole backgrounds. When that data arrived (Roman 1986 per MMV; MMV 2017; APT 2019), Type IV turned out to occur for quantum test fields. M's hypothesis therefore holds for the catalogue claim, but it cuts against the tree's sentence ('nothing known'), not against the published 'no known classical field', which still stands. MMV 2021 then added back-reaction data, which narrows the other way: Type IV is excluded in static exteriors, on Killing horizons and on stationary axes. For the application, the tree lacked Le's full-wall measurement and a metric carrying the bubble's motion. With both supplied here, 'Type-IV dominated at v_s = 0.5' does not move: 98.84 % against Le's 98.7 %, and 7/7 at the sampled points. What moves is the printed numbers (they belong to a different metric), 'anywhere' (about 1.2 % of the wall is not Type IV), and 'orthogonal' (Type IV implies NEC violation). Evidence the other way: the Type IV fraction falls with speed, and the Rodal profile is Type I, so Type IV is a property of the curl-bearing Alcubierre/Natario class, not of warp metrics in general. The tree's 'Alcubierre class' scoping (typefour.py:73-76) is correct on that point.
audits.grade_evidence: The external content STANDS. The taxonomy re-derives: Type IV has complex eigenvalues, no causal eigenvector, and violates every standard energy condition (C1, sympy + z3). The Alcubierre application re-derives on the true metric: 7/7 wall points are Type IV, and the wall fraction is 98.84 % against Le's 98.7 % at identical parameters (C2, C5). The grade is NARROWED because the tree uses the result on a larger class than the sources support. (1) typefour.py:15, :20 'NOTHING KNOWN IS TYPE IV' drops the 'classical' qualifier; the Unruh quantum vacuum is Type IV (2102.13551; 1607.05280). (2) typefour.py:57-63 'orthogonal' contradicts the implication Type IV => NEC violated (z3 unsat). (3) typefour.py:18 and anec.py:71 globalise a pointwise type, while about 1.2-1.3 % of the wall is not Type IV. (4) anec.py:70/:210 'D-independent' is tested at one point and one sigma; measured over sigma 4-32, Type IV persists (99.1 % to 95.6 %) but the fraction is not invariant. Two discrepancies are recorded, not repaired, and neither is a refutation. First, typefour.py:108-110/:138 computes a static metric that is not Alcubierre's (Ricci scalar differs at 6 of 7 points, and the BBV validation is blind to it), yet the Type IV label survives at every point. Second, 'Le's Table 1' corresponds to 2602.18023v6 Table 2 in the versions read. Nothing is WRONG. anec.py's actual check, is_type_iv((0.9,0.3,0)), is also true on the correct metric (0.2815).
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree scopes its sentences to 'no known classical matter', 'Type-IV dominated wall' and 'orthogonal to averaged and magnitude conditions', and computes the moving-bubble metric. The classification cannot become WRONG. The Alcubierre label would be WRONG only if an interval-certified evaluation found the wall predominantly Type I at v_s = 0.5, sigma = 8, which neither Le's numerics nor the 30-digit evaluation here supports. Reading 2102.13551 sec 3.5 (p.17) would settle whether the on-axis Type IV found here falls outside MMV's hypotheses. audits.published_statement:
AMM, Sec. III p.10, verbatim and re-read live: 'A necessary condition for the validity of the large N semi-classical equations of motion (2.9) is that the linear response equations (3.4) should have no solutions with finite non-singular initial data for which any linearized gauge invariant scalar quantity grows without bound.' (3.4) is obtained 'around a given semi-classical geometry g_ab that solves eq.(2.9)' (p.8). Pi^(ret) is 'evaluated in the background geometry of the leading order solution of the semi-classical equations (2.9)' (p.9). On flat space AMM write that it 'is stable to all perturbations on distance scales much larger than the Planck length' (abstract) and that 'flat spacetime is completely infrared stable in semi-classical gravity' (p.4). On k = 0 global modes: 'We do not treat this possibility' (p.12). They call the criterion 'a necessary, though perhaps not a sufficient condition' (p.13).

GMMPS state 'the linear instability of the semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon system linearised about the Minkowski vacuum' (abstract). Thm 3.6 gives alpha~^S_1 = 1/(64 pi^2) and alpha~^TT_1 = 0. Thm 4.16 (p.58): 'If Z subset (-4m^2, 0) and if S in C_c^inf(M), the solution ... are bounded in time ... If Z subset (-4m^2, inf), with some gamma in Z, gamma > 0, the solution is exponentially growing', with Z the zero set of Q(w^2). 5.1: 'there are two negative numbers q_2 < q_1 < 0 such that, if b_2 < 0 ... in all these cases, there is a zero gamma_0 of F_S that it is real valued and that is slightly smaller than 0 ... For sufficiently large -b_2, this is the only negative zero that can be found in D.' 5.2.1: 'This different behaviour [from Anderson et al.] is originated by the choice of the renormalisation parameters done in Theorem 3.6.' 5.3: gamma~ ~ -b_0/b_1 = -16 pi G alpha~^S_1 m^4, H = sqrt(-gamma~), m ~ 7.8e-3 eV.
published_hypotheses: AMM A1: the background g_ab SOLVES the large-N semiclassical equations (2.9) in a state |in>. (3.4) is its first variation, and Pi^(ret) is evaluated on that solution (pp.8-9, live).
AMM A2: the matter is large-N free quantum fields. The flat example uses a scalar of arbitrary mass m > 0 and coupling xi in the Minkowski vacuum.
AMM A3: only gauge-invariant scalars built from h_ab count, and gauge transformations (3.11) that change the action (2.7) are excluded (p.10).
AMM A4: renormalised Lambda, 1/G_N, alpha and beta are defined by subtractions at k^2 = 0 (4.4).
AMM A5 (flat result): the fourth-order coefficients are O(1), so new modes appear only at G_N|k^2| ~ 1. k = 0 global scalar modes are not treated (p.12).

AMM A6: the tensor sector assumes beta non-negative, i.e. 16 pi G_N beta k^2 + 1 > 0 (4.6), p.11. The scalar result rests on the log growth (4.11), whose coefficient may vanish, e.g. at xi = 1/6. The criterion is necessary, not sufficient (p.13).
GMMPS G1: ONE real Klein-Gordon field, m > 0, and xi with 2/(6 xi - 1) < 4 (5.1).
GMMPS G2: background (R^4, eta) in the Poincare vacuum; past-compact forcing problem; de Donder gauge.
GMMPS G3: alpha~^S_1 = 1/(64 pi^2) and alpha~^TT_1 = 0 (Thm 3.6). alpha~^S_2 = alpha~^TT_2 = 0 is assumed.
GMMPS G4: Thm 4.16 needs a REAL zero set: bounded if Z is in (-4m^2, 0); growth if Z is in (-4m^2, inf) with some zero > 0. Complex zeros are not covered.
GMMPS G5: universality of H needs alpha~^S_3 large and negative and alpha~^TT_4 large and positive (5.2.1). 5.1 phrases the condition as 'large -b_2', while 5.2 and 5.3 use 'b_2 positive and large'.
GMMPS G6: 5.3 neglects J and takes b_1 >> the other constants.
